title: WT-Fault-LLM:Knowledge Graph Enhanced Large Model for Wind-turbine Faults
abstract: This study introduces an innovative framework integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with knowledge graphs to significantly enhance wind turbine fault diagnosis, specifically addressing critical LLM limitations in industrial settings, such as knowledge inaccuracies and deficiencies in symbolic reasoning. While LLMs exhibit proficiency in general domains, their application in specialized vertical fields remains constrained. Knowledge graphs offer a solution by providing structured, interpretable reasoning through networks of triplets. The proposed architecture employs a three-layer "knowledge storage-retrieval-generation reasoning" structure to integrate heterogeneous data sources—including wind turbine manuals and maintenance records—into a domain-specific knowledge graph that explicitly models fault entities, their attributes, and causal relationships. A novel dual-channel semantic retrieval mechanism is implemented, concurrently leveraging graph-based reasoning paths within the knowledge graph and semantic similarity matching via a vector database, thereby substantially improving adaptability to complex operational scenarios. Utilizing local deployment with the DeepSeek-R1 model and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques, the framework transforms both structured and unstructured data into contextual constraints through dynamic prompt engineering, resulting in markedly improved fault diagnosis accuracy. Case studies establish the system’s capacity for sophisticated multi-hop causal reasoning, such as identifying that "gearbox noise" can originate from underlying causes like lubricant contamination. Future research will prioritize the integration of multi-modal data, including vibration spectrums, to accelerate the transformation of industrial operations from experience-based practices to knowledge-driven methodologies. This work provides a valuable technical paradigm for the reliable application of LLMs in vertical industrial domains.

title: XChronos Temporal Framework for AGI v1.0
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Modern AI systems lack a genuine temporal substrate. Although large language models operate on token sequences, they do not maintain meaningful events, recurrence structures, episodic continuity, or internal state evolution. This absence prevents long-term learning, identity formation, narrative coherence, and other minimal requirements for Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). This document introduces the XChronos Temporal Framework for AGI, a formal temporal ontology composed of four symbolic primitives — Crônons, Hexacronons, Metacronons, and Autocronons — combined with the symbolic value token Hexa (ɧ), a validation mechanism (Proof-of-Recurrence), and a declarative semantic language (XSL). Together, these components provide an internal temporal architecture enabling AGI to track significance, detect recurrence, integrate patterns, update internal state, and record human–AI co-generated insights over time. The XChronos Framework does not describe a theory of mind or neuroscience metaphor. It is a structural engineering protocol designed to supply continuity, memory, and temporal coherence to artificial cognitive systems.

title: Z-SPACE: A MULTI-AGENT TOOL ORCHESTRATION FRAMEWORK FOR ENTERPRISE-GRADE LLM AUTOMATION
ZEAL – A Framework for Zero-Shot Enhanced Analysis and Learning for SEM Image Defect Correction in ICs
abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing encompasses a variety of precision-oriented processes, including deep ultraviolet (DUV) and extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, plasma etching, atomic layer deposition (ALD), and chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), all essential for producing high-density integrated circuits (ICs). As the dimensions of transistors continue to decrease, defects like line-edge roughness (LER), micro-voids, metal bridging, and pattern collapse become progressively harder to identify and correct, adversely affecting yield and reliability. Conventional optical inspection and rule-based defect classification systems, while proficient in detecting larger anomalies, often struggle to identify subtle process-induced defects at advanced technology nodes due to limitations in resolution and variations in processes [1]. Even though supervised deep learning models, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs), have shown remarkable accuracy in classifying defects, their dependency on extensive labeled datasets poses a considerable challenge, especially for new defect modes in state-of-the-art semiconductor processes. To address these challenges, zero-shot learning (ZSL) emerges as a compelling alternative by utilizing self-supervised or contrastive learning models, including CLIP, SimCLR, and DINO, which can adapt to previously unseen defect categories by differentiating between normal and anomalous patterns without the need for large amounts of labeled data [2]. However, detection alone does not rectify manufacturing defects—engineers are also required to identify root causes and formulate corrective actions, a task that remains predominantly manual and labor-intensive. Generative AI methodologies, such as diffusion models, autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks (GANs), can recreate absent or flawed features, providing valuable insights into optimal defect-free configurations [3]. Furthermore, large language models (LLMs) improve interpretability by generating textual elucidations, performing root cause analyses, and offering actionable suggestions for process optimization [4]. By integrating zero-shot detection, generative AI-driven defect remediation, and LLM-enhanced reasoning, our proposed framework for “Zero-Shot Enhanced Analysis and Learning for SEM Image Defect Correction in ICs” or ZEAL framework evolves from merely identifying defects to establishing an automated decision-making system. Our proposed ZEAL framework (as illustrated in Fig. 1) improves the detection and remediation of defects through a well-defined four-stage process: (1) SEM Image Acquisition and Preprocessing, (2) Zero-Shot Defect Detection, (3) Generative AI-Assisted Defect Correction, and (4) LLM-Based Reasoning and Recommendations. Although the methodology is fundamentally node-agnostic, enhancements are necessary to optimize feature recognition across various technology nodes. SEM Image Acquisition and Preprocessing: T

title: ZeroCAP: Zero-Shot Multi-Robot Context Aware Pattern Formation via Large Language Models
venue: Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings
abstract: Incorporating language comprehension into robotic operations unlocks significant advancements in robotics, but also presents distinct challenges, particularly in executing spatially oriented tasks like pattern formation. This paper introduces ZeroCAP, a novel system that integrates large language models with multi-robot systems for zero-shot context aware pattern formation. Grounded in the principles of language-conditioned robotics, ZeroCAP leverages the interpretative power of language models to translate natural language instructions into actionable robotic configurations. This approach combines the synergy of vision-language models, cutting-edge segmentation techniques and shape descriptors, enabling the realization of complex, context-driven pattern formations in the realm of multi robot coordination. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate the systems proficiency in executing complex context aware pattern formations across a spectrum of tasks, from surrounding and caging objects to infilling regions. This not only validates the system's capability to interpret and implement intricate context-driven tasks but also underscores its adaptability and effectiveness across varied environments and scenarios. The experimental videos and additional information about this work can be found at https://sites.google.com/view/zerocap/home.

title: Онтологический язык разницы: наблюдатель, время, информация (версия вторая, дополненная)
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The article proposes an ontological language in which time, information, and the observer are defined as structures of difference, rather than as substances. The model belongs to the tradition of relational and processual approaches in the philosophy of physics — relational quantum mechanics (Carlo Rovelli), QBism (Christopher Fuchs), process philosophy (Alfred North Whitehead), and information theory (Gregory Bateson) — and offers a unified terminological synthesis of this tradition. Segmentation of statements by epistemic status: each substantive paragraph in Sections 4–7 is tagged: [Language] — a metaphor or instrument of description, not a physical statement. [Re-description] — a new way of speaking about an already known fact, without new explanation. [Hypothesis] — a statement admitting verification; where possible, the method is indicated. [Fact] — relies on a generally accepted, reproducible scientific result. The article does not claim to solve open problems in physics (the Hubble constant discrepancy, the nature of dark matter, the origin of early supermassive black holes). The applications presented in Section 4 are partly re-descriptions of already known facts in a new vocabulary, and partly testable hypotheses. The terms «multiverse» and «absolute» are used in an ontological sense — as a space of potential interpretations and the limit of applicability of language — and not as cosmological or physical entities. The only part of the model admitting direct verification already now is Section 5.4, which proposes a protocol for comparing the responses of language models with and without an ontological framework. The conducted experiment (N=10 responses (5 questions × 2 modes) from Claude, with control measurements on Kimi, DeepSeek, and Grok) shows that the use of an ontological core increases the ontological consistency (Ontological Consistency Score, OCS) of responses by an average of 36.7% compared to baseline indicators (from 18.0 to 24.6 points out of 25 possible). This is the first empirical result confirming the practical value of the proposed ontological language as a tool of prompt engineering. The application of this language to the problem of superintelligence safety is presented in a separate work by the author (Arslanova, 2026b). Keywords: ontology of information, observer, difference, large language models (LLMs), symbol grounding, quantum decoherence, prompt engineering, ontological consistency.

title: 差异即功能:全球大模型语义域共建倡议

abstract: 中文摘要: 本文在《龙序·序存·存续先于存在公理体系》框架下,提出一项关于全球大模型语义域共建的倡议,正文自包含,不预设读者已读其他论文。文章先立其意:语义域是正在凝结的文明认知基础设施,真正的治理对象不是单个模型的行为,而是所有模型共同凝结出的概念空间本身;多元而非单一的凝结,不仅能避免文明被锁入单一错误结构,更能带来认知韧性、方案空间放大、互构生最大化与意义纵深保全四项正向结果。基于此,本文主张将结构性差异本身确立为偏差检测与意义生成的双重功能组件——“差异即功能”,给出可操作的全球大模型语义域共建八项原则,并进一步补全其可执行性:执行架构(共建理事会)、断路器设计(触发与执行路径)、视角独立性的底层威胁(设计者认知框架)、多元凝结的失败模式,以及起步路径(最小可行版本)。全文属《龙序》体系的衍生思考(体系产出),概念与论证均在正文内联定义,本体论判断独立成立于《龙序》体系。文末以作者主观立场收束:语义域的布局结构将影响下一次科技大爆发的节点。本文不涉及具体工程实现的技术细节。八项原则的设计基于存在论层面的结构需求,而非现有工程能力的限制。具体实现路径留待后续技术与工程共同体共同探索。 英文摘要: Under the "Sequenced Existence · Existence Before Survival" axiom system (the LongOrder framework), this paper proposes a global initiative for the co-construction of the semantic domain of large language models. The paper argues that the true governance target is not the behavior of individual models, but the conceptual space jointly condensed by all models. Plural rather than monolithic condensation not only prevents civilization from being locked into a single erroneous structure, but also yields four positive outcomes: cognitive resilience, solution-space amplification, maximization of mutual construction, and preservation of semantic depth. Based on this, the paper establishes structural difference itself as a dual functional component for both bias detection and meaning generation—"Difference as Function"—and presents eight actionable principles for global semantic domain co-construction, supplemented by executive architecture (co-construction council), circuit breaker design (trigger and execution paths), the underlying threat to viewpoint independence (designer cognitive frame), failure modes of plural condensation, and a minimal viable path. This paper does not address specific engineering implementation details; the eight principles are designed based on ontological structural requirements rather than current engineering capabilities. The author concludes with a subjective stance: the layout structure of the semantic domain will influence the node of the next technological great leap. 关键词

title: ПУТИ И ПЕРСПЕКТИВЫ ИСПОЛЬЗОВАНИЯ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТУАЛЬНЬГХ АГЕНТОВ В КОСМОНАВТИКЕ
abstract: В статье рассматриваются перспективы применения интеллектуальных агентов на базе больших языковых моделей в космонавтике и космическом приборостроении. Выделены ключевые направления: ИИ-ассистенты в проектировании (включая RAG-подходы, CAD/САПР и генеративный дизайн), анализ надежности и предиктивное техническое обслуживание на основе телеметрии и цифровых двойников, интеллектуальная робототехника для автономных миссий, а также ИИ-помощники для экипажей и обучения персонала. Отдельное внимание уделено применению БЯМ в разработке бортового программного обеспечения и в работе с требованиями к критическим системам, предлагается принцип «ИИ предлагает - человек утверждает - математика доказывает» с акцентом на формализацию требований, трассируемость, генерацию тестов и интеграцию с формальными методами верификации. Обсуждаются риски внедрения (галлюцинации, недетерминизм, конфиденциальность, требования к вычислительным ресурсам) и меры их снижения, включая строгий RAG, локальное развертывание моделей и обязательную экспертизу человеком. The presented article discusses prospects for using intelligent agents based on large language models (LLMs) in space exploration. Key application areas are outlined: AI assistants for engineering design (including RAG, CAD workflows, and generative design), reliability analysis and predictive maintenance using telemetry and digital twins, intelligent robotics for highly autonomous missions, and onboard AI assistants for crews and personnel training. Special attention is paid to applying LLM-based agents to onboard software engineering and requirements engineering for safety-critical systems; the paper proposes the principle "AI proposes - human approves - mathematics proves," emphasizing requirements clarification and formalization, traceability management, test generation, and integration with formal verification methods. The paper also analyzes limitations and risks (hallucinations, non-determinism, confidentiality constraints, and computing requirements) and describes mitigation approaches such as strict RAG, on-premise deployment, and mandatory human expert review.

abstract: In the contemporary landscape of Software Engineering and Business Process Management (BPM), the integration of generative artificial intelligence has precipitated a paradigm shift from manual, deterministic specification to automated, probabilistic generation. While offering scalability, this transition introduces a fundamental volatility known as the "Probabilistic Gap"—the chasm between the fluid, high-variance output of Large Language Models (LLMs) and the strict, zero-tolerance syntactic requirements of execution engines like DMN (Decision Model and Notation). This paper addresses the "Struc-Bench Paradox," highlighting the limitations of transformer architectures in generating complex structured data without rigid orchestration. The study formally defines and implements the "Dispatcher," a pivotal control plane component designed to function as an intelligent resource arbiter and quality gatekeeper within a neuro-symbolic architecture. The theoretical framework shifts the economic focus from Baumol’s Cost Disease, which addresses production speed, to Boehm’s Law of Software Economics, which emphasizes the exponential cost of defects propagated to production. To operationalize this, the Dispatcher represents a discrete deterministic process modeled using Cost-Colored Petri Nets rather than Finite State Machines (FSMs). The Petri Net formalism allows for precise modeling of concurrency, state accumulation, and the strict enforcement of "Retry Budgets," thereby mathematically guaranteeing system termination and preventing infinite loops of costly regeneration. The architectural implementation utilizes a "Test-First" generation philosophy: the system first synthesizes validation criteria (JSON test cases) utilizing Schema Injection and RAG, and subsequently grounds the generation of DMN logic (XML) in these pre-validated scenarios. Experimental analysis was conducted using a controlled set of 200 generation cycles to evaluate two distinct error-recovery strategies: Strategy A (Independent regeneration of DMN tables only) and Strategy B (Joint/Dynamic regeneration of both DMN and Test Cases). Quantitative results demonstrate that Strategy B is economically superior, achieving a 6.06% reduction in total cost and an 8.44% reduction in token consumption compared to the independent patching approach. The findings indicate that simultaneous regeneration empowers the LLM to resolve semantic incoherence and hallucinations more effectively than iterative repairs, prioritizing logical consistency over partial code retention. abstract: This thesis addresses the need for more adaptive and user-centered operator-support systems in modern manufacturing environments. Its main objective is to investigate how Augmented Reality (AR) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be combined into a unified framework capable of supporting human operators during collaborative industrial tasks while reducing cognitive burden, interaction complexity, and the likelihood of errors. To achieve this objective, a layered framework was designed and implemented, integrating AR-based interfaces, AI-driven perception modules, multimodal interaction methods, orchestration services, and robotic communication. The proposed system includes contextual visual guidance, gesture- and voice-based interaction, IMU-based task\ completion detection, and LLM-supported communication, all developed under a user centric design methodology. The framework was demonstrated through a case study involving electrical cabinet assembly in a human–robot collaborative setting. Its evaluation was performed through three complementary procedures: qualitative comparison with state-of-the-art frameworks, user testing in a laboratory environment, and KPI-based quantitative assessment. The results indicate that the proposed framework provides meaningful benefits in terms of usability, workflow continuity, assembly guidance, error prevention, and operator support, while also highlighting its potential for improving efficiency, ergonomics, and collaboration in manufacturing environments.

title: 10 Funding Applications: A Phase 1, First-in Human, PDAC Clinical Trial Protocol of a LLM-Directed Robotic Whipple with Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236)
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: In July 2026 the White House asked the federal research portfolio, approximately $200 billion annually, to prioritise the individual scientist over legacy institutions. This paper reports what happens when one unaffiliated scientist takes that literally and writes ten funding applications for the same Phase 1 pancreatic cancer trial, each addressing the mechanism its recipient runs. The trial is constant across all ten: an open-label, single-arm, 3+3 escalation of perioperative daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) in up to 18 participants with resectable or borderline-resectable KRAS G12-mutated pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, performed as a staged eight-arm robotic pancreaticoduodenectomy with an on-premises language model confined to advisory output. Five lead with the operation and five with the drug; both sets describe the same hybrid procedure. UC San Diego Moores Cancer Center is named in all ten as the intended partner of choice, at the feasibility stage only, and described nowhere as a partner, sponsor, site, or endorser. The evidence is stated with its limits attached. An August 2025 quantitative systems pharmacology simulation returned median overall survival of 12.8 months against 5.4 for chemotherapy; in May 2026 RASolute 302 reported 13.2 against 6.6 months in the RAS G12 metastatic population. That proximity is chronology, not validation, and neither result speaks to resectable setting, which is what trial would measure.

title: 114‐2: Computer Vision and Agentic AI – New Paradigm Shift for Display Applications and Manufacturing
venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers
abstract: While computer vision designed to study and represent the human visual system has achieved significant milestones with deep learning technology in face recognition, defect detection, and image enhancement. There are still several limitations such as the long‐tail problem, scaling issues, transfer learning, and cross‐domain generalization hinder broad practical deployment. In display manufacturing applications, a major bottleneck is the heavy reliance on well‐structured data for supervised learning; high accuracy labeled images for defects are not only insufficient in quantity but also prohibitively expensive to collect. Consequently, state‐of‐the‐art systems often fail in ways that humans do not, there is an urgent need to build systems that produce more human‐aligned behavior. Since 2021, Large Language Models (LLMs) and Agentic AI have undergone remarkable advancements, driving transformative developments across diverse domains such as natural language understanding, multimodal generation, and human‐AI interaction. Capitalizing on this emerging multimodal paradigm, both industry and academia are increasingly exploring how general‐purpose foundation models can be adapted to domain‐specific challenges. By leveraging their exceptional generalization capabilities, deep semantic reasoning, and zero‐or few‐shot adaptability, researchers are developing more efficient and robust AI agents for real world applications. In this paper, we explore the implications of this new paradigm for the display industry. We propose Tri‐Agent framework oriented multimodal models to address long‐standing, high‐impact challenges in the display manufacturing industry, specifically, automated defect detection, automated action recognition for operator guidance, and high‐fidelity 3D content generation for design and simulation. These results demonstrate that composing AI agent with vision‐language model is both more efficient and more effective than existing methods, paving the way for practical and scalable tool‐augmented systems.

title: 2d_min The Minimum Topological Structural Unit: A First-Principles Framework for Lossless Neural Network Reconstruction and Holographic Virtual Data Storage
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Abstract Modern deep learning architectures — particularly Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) — and high-dimensional data management systems face severe bottlenecks from O(N2) attention scaling and memory footprint. We suggest these inefficiencies may stem from a potential mismatch between “continuous high-dimensional vector representations / explicit three-dimensional spatial grid coordinates” and the “discrete topological structure of the underlying logical information.” Starting from the general principle that information is relational — arising from distinguishable relations between objects rather than being an intrinsic property of an isolated object — we independently derive the 2dmin Minimum Topological Structural Unit axiom: the minimum span at which two indivisible minimum spatial units first establish a distinguishable relation is 2dmin. We further use the Bekenstein–Hawking black-hole entropy formula and the holographic principle from quantum gravity as an independent cross-scale theoretical corroboration, showing that this axiom is mutually consistent with the physical result that “storing 1 Bit of entropy requires at least 4 Planck areas,” which offers preliminary support for its universality under extreme physical boundary conditions. We further propose an untested hypothesis: that parameter, input, and storage-coordinate fluctuations below the dmin scale may represent “unmanifest noise” lacking relational topology. Around this hypothesis, the paper constructs a possible reconstruction scheme — restructuring parameter space into a discrete topological lattice, condensing fragmented input tokens into holographic phase units, and mapping high-dimensional virtual storage onto a 4dmin2 two-dimensional holographic boundary array — as a possible route toward eliminating continuous floating-point noise, compressing memory and weight footprint, and reducing spatial-coordinate (x, y, z) addressing overhead. The paper's aim is to propose a logically self-consistent, falsifiable first-principles theoretical framework together with a concrete set of testable hypotheses (Section 5), not to report already-realized or already-validated engineering results; the actual magnitude of any engineering benefit awaits confirmation by future experiments.

title: 3D visual grounding based on active perception
abstract: 3D visual grounding (3DVG) is a key capability for embodied agents, requiring a robot to localize in 3D the object referred to by a free-form language expression. Existing LLM/VLM-based approaches often make one-shot decisions from incomplete observations or invoke expensive multimodal reasoning over the full scene, leading to ambiguous grounding, hallucinatory predictions, and limited reliability. We address this challenge by formulating 3DVG as state-driven closed-loop grounding over a reusable scene memory. Given a query decomposed into a context-ordered grounding sequence, our framework maintains the current candidate set and accumulated structured evidence, predicts informative viewpoints for active perception, and performs candidate-conditioned verification only within the projected local region of the predicted view. Newly acquired observations are sparsely written back to scene memory, enabling local memory recovery and candidate refresh without global recomputation. We further introduce a feedback-driven re-grounding mechanism with resolved, ambiguous, missing, and conflict states: the system advances only when a unique candidate is verified; otherwise, it continues active perception or backtracks to recover upstream anchors. By using the VLM only for candidate verification while reading final 3D geometry from scene memory, and by confining high-cost multimodal reasoning to active local candidates, the proposed framework improves robustness under partial observability and mitigates hallucination risk. Experiments on ScanRefer, Sr3D, Nr3D, and OpenTarget demonstrate the effectiveness of our method and show strong performance against competitive baselines.

title: 68‐2: Research on AI Agent in the Display Industry
venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers
abstract: To promote the intelligent transformation of the display manufacturing industry, this paper summarizes the Deep Research Agent (DR Agent) based on Large Language Models (LLMs), which is one of the current research hotspots. Centered on in‐depth knowledge mining, complex task decomposition, and closed‐loop optimization, this agent technology addresses key industry pain points such as data silos and efficiency bottlenecks. The paper elaborates on its four core architectures, optimization methods, and implementation logic. Meanwhile, it discusses the credibility of DR Agent in scenarios including equipment operation and maintenance, fault diagnosis, and constructs a closed loop of “application ‐ accumulation ‐ optimization”.

title: 6G, 3GPP and Europe's Next Security Frontier: Who Has Final Authority in AI-Native Networks?
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: 6G changes the security question 6G will not simply be a faster 5G. It is expected to bring artificial intelligence, sensing, cloud, robotics and communications much more deeply together. The European Commission itself describes 6G as expanding integrated sensing and communication as well as artificial intelligence, while emphasising security, resilience, interoperability and European technological sovereignty as strategic objectives. 3GPP's technical programme is already moving in this direction. Release 20 includes work on AI/ML for NG-RAN, AI/ML management, enhanced core-network support for AI/ML, and security for core-network AI/ML support. Most strikingly, 3GPP created TR 29.832, “Study on the Protocol for Artificial Intelligence in 6G,” under CT3 in June 2026. This means the important question is no longer simply whether AI will participate in future communication infrastructure. It will. The harder question is: When an AI system generates a network operation, what makes that operation authoritative enough to become a real network consequence? An AI system may calculate a beam change. It may recommend a handover. It may select a routing modification. It may initiate a network API operation. It may determine that telemetry should be exported. It may propose admission to a network slice. But none of those computations necessarily answers a different question: Should this exact operation, with these exact parameters, be allowed to become effective now? That distinction can be expressed simply: Computation is not authority. Where the world stands today Much of the international competition around AI-native communications is understandably centred on three areas: AI capability, semiconductor and infrastructure capability, and standards influence. Europe is also investing substantially in this race. The EU's Smart Networks and Services Joint Undertaking has a mission to foster European technological sovereignty in 6G, and in 2026 Europe announced another €116 million for twenty 6G research and innovation projects as part of a much larger portfolio. Those investments are important. But there is another dimension of sovereignty that deserves equal attention. Current security architecture is extremely good at answering questions such as: Who is the user? Which network function is authenticated? Which workload is permitted to communicate? What API may it call? What policy applies? What network state exists? What should be logged? What should be denied? AI-native infrastructure introduces an additional question: Who controls the transition from a machine-generated decision into an actual network consequence? That is not identical to authentication. It is not identical to authorization. It is not identical to AI safety. And it is not identical to logging or audit. It concerns execution authority itself. title: A Bi-Directional Production Monitoring System with LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract: Process visibility is a key enabler of smart manufacturing, and production monitoring advances this aim through systematic data collection and analysis. However, current systems face challenges including difficulties in integrating non-structured and multimodal data, reliance on expert knowledge for complex task analysis, and passive, inflexible user interfaces that impede effective decision-making. This study introduces a Bi-Directional Production Monitoring System (BiPMS) leveraging agentic Large Language Models (LLMs) within a multi-agent collaboration framework. Specifically, the Manufacturing Process Integration (MPI) Module automatically maps process information into a structured format, while the Cognitive Decision Support (CDS) Module translates complex production monitoring tasks in natural language into tangible actions. Consequently, production knowledge generated during these processes can be registered, applied, and continuously updated. A case study on steel rail manufacturing, including the implementation of a prototype system and comparative analysis, indicates the framework’s effectiveness in improving production monitoring and managing manufacturing knowledge.

title: A Bibliometric Analysis on the Integration of Large Language Models and Knowledge Graphs
venue: Revista de Informática Teórica e Aplicada
abstract: In recent years, the integration of large language models and knowledge graphs has increasingly attracted the attention of both researchers and practitioners. While existing reviews provide valuable and helpful insights for better understanding the research field, they lack a quantitative perspective. To address this limitation, a bibliometric analysis was performed in this study to fill the gap. In particular, sourcing data from the Web of Science and Scopus databases, our analysis focuses on: (1) publication and citation trends, (2) the most productive countries and authors, (3) the most influential sources and scientific papers, (4) the main research tasks particularly in KG-enhanced LLMs and LLM-augmented KGs, (5) the most frequently employed techniques and their evolution over time. In addition to providing a comprehensive overview of the most active and recent areas of research, this study identifies several emerging themes, namely: “Knowledge-aware Prompt Engineering”, “Retrieval-Augmented Generation for LLM–KG Integration”, “Knowledge Graph-based Hallucination Detection” and the convergence of “Multimodal Knowledge Graphs and Multimodal Large Language Models”. These insights contribute to a clearer understanding of the field's development and highlight emerging research trends grounded in bibliometric evidence.

title: A BIM-Integrated ANN–LSTM–RAG Framework for Intelligent Predictive Maintenance and Automated FMEA Generation in HVAC Systems
abstract: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems play a critical role in modern buildings, making effective predictive maintenance essential for improving operational efficiency and reducing maintenance costs. However, existing approaches generally address Building Information Modeling (BIM), equipment degradation prediction, and maintenance decision support as independent tasks. This study proposes a BIM-integrated ANN–LSTM–RAG framework that combines Industry Foundation Classes (IFC)-based semantic information, hybrid Artificial Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (ANN–LSTM) degradation prediction, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to automate Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) for HVAC systems. IFC-derived semantic information is combined with operational sensor data to predict equipment degradation, while retrieved engineering knowledge generates structured FMEA reports and maintenance recommendations. Experimental evaluation demonstrated an RMSE of 4.1%, a prediction accuracy of 95.0%, and a RAGAS score of 0.917. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating BIM semantics, hybrid deep learning, and retrieval-augmented reasoning to support intelligent predictive maintenance and facility management.

title: A Build-or-Buy AI Case in the Public Sector: Augmenting a Canadian Asset-Mapping Platform with LLM and Ontology Capabilities
abstract: ConnectON is a Canadian asset-mapping platform operated as a shared municipal service by a not-forprofit alliance, holding over 125,000 business records and serving more than 300 municipal staff and partners across the agri-food, manufacturing, and tourism sectors. In considering whether to augment its search function with generative AI, specifically a large language model complemented by ontologies, the platform confronted a build-versus-buy decision that, in a public-sector context, is governed by considerations beyond predictive accuracy. Data sovereignty, cost sustainability, data access restrictions, and integration with live infrastructure each constrain the choice. A cloud-based LLM offers strong performance but transmits sensitive queries to an external provider and creates exposure to vendor lock-in, whereas a selfhosted open-weights LLM retains both the data and the AI capability internally. Across 201 test cases spanning 11 architectures, a local open-weights model paired with ontology-aware retrieval performed within a single exact match of the cloud benchmark, strongly supporting an in-house approach.

title: A Business-Level Cognitive Framework for Regulation of Autonomous Digital Agents and Growth of Distributed Intelligence
venue: European International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Management Studies
abstract: The increasing deployment of autonomous digital agents across enterprise ecosystems has introduced a structural transformation in how organizations regulate decision-making, distribute intelligence, and manage operational autonomy. These agents, embedded within digital twins, virtual environments, and distributed computing systems, are increasingly responsible for real-time decision execution, adaptive coordination, and self-regulated task management. However, the absence of a structured business-level cognitive framework has led to governance fragmentation, reduced interpretability, and limited scalability in multi-agent ecosystems. This research proposes a business-level cognitive framework designed to regulate autonomous digital agents while enabling the structured growth of distributed intelligence across enterprise environments. The framework integrates cognitive governance principles, multi-agent coordination theory, and digital twin-based operational modeling to create a layered architecture for scalable autonomy. Foundational insights are drawn from multi-agent systems theory (Wooldridge, 2009), generative social simulation models (Epstein, 2006), and agent-based innovation diffusion structures (Terna, 2009), which collectively inform the cognitive structuring of distributed intelligence ecosystems. Additionally, the study incorporates industrial digital twin and extended reality frameworks (Burghardt et al., 2020; Calandra et al., 2024; Feddoul et al., 2023) to establish a real-time interaction layer between physical and virtual enterprise environments. These systems are further complemented by interoperable architectures based on OPC-UA standards and virtual pedagogical simulation environments (Havard et al., 2023), enabling synchronized cognitive feedback loops across distributed agents. A central theoretical anchor of this work is the enterprise agentic governance framework proposed by Venkiteela (2026), which defines scalable autonomy, structured oversight layers, and cognitive regulation mechanisms for autonomous digital systems. This framework is extended in this research to introduce a business-level cognitive control model that aligns organizational decision structures with distributed agent intelligence.

title: A CAD- and Chain-of-Thought-Based Robot-Teaching Dataset for Structured Manufacturing Task Representation and Verification
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based robot planning is a promising direction for manufacturing automation, but the available learning resources are still dominated by visual observations, natural-language annotations, or action trajectories. These modalities do not by themselves provide an explicit, machine-readable account of manufacturing-equipment geometry, kinematic relationships, process constraints, and the rationale connecting a task state to a selected high-level action. This paper presents a CAD- and Chain-of-Thought (CoT)-based robot-teaching dataset for structured manufacturing task representation and verification. A reproducible semi-automated pipeline converts STEP models into STL and Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) representations, associates them with robot-state time series, and organizes the task rationale into four stages: Perception, Reasoning, Decision, and Execution. In this dataset, the Execution stage is a high-level action specification with expected preconditions and postconditions; it is not a joint trajectory, controller command, or direct robot-policy output. The dataset contains 120 CAD-based environment models, 360 robot-state sequences, and 480 instruction–answer samples, with a 25%/75% real/virtual composition. Four public 7B–8B-parameter LLMs are fine-tuned under identical quantized low-rank adaptation settings. Evaluation is limited to two representation-level tasks: URDF spatial question answering and CoT task-procedure consistency verification. In the full-data setting, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct obtains 99.71% URDF spatial-QA accuracy and 99.84% CoT-verification accuracy (1236/1238 decisions; precision, recall, and F1-score = 0.9985). These item-level scores quantify structured understanding and consistency verification and must not be interpreted as robot task-success rates. Component ablations show gains of 66.71 percentage points for URDF spatial QA and 53.94 percentage points for CoT consistency verification. The results support the dataset as a structured resource for explainable, traceable, and independently verifiable manufacturing-task representations, while end-to-end trajectory generation and physical task-success validation remain future work. The dataset is publicly available on AI Hub at https://aihub.or.kr/aihubdata/data/view.do?dataSetSn=71937

title: A Calculus of Discernment: Decision-Relevant Insight, Sequence Value, and Forgetting as Higher-Order Learning
abstract: In a world of generative AI, candidate insights are abundant; what is scarce is the capacity to discern which matter, to act on them in the right amount and order, and to forget the rest so the system can adapt. We argue these scarcities are governed by one object and build a framework around it. We define an insight strictly as a lever with an identified, measurable effect on an objective, and rank candidates by decision-relevance via the expected value of information rather than novelty. We show action carries an order, not only a size: under realistic belief dynamics, content "touches" are non-commuting operators, so a fixed plan delivered in different orders yields different outcomes, defining a sequence premium. We observe that the value of any lever is a shadow price, unifying pharmaceutical marketing, equity selection, and manufacturing as one leverage-discovery problem. Most speculatively, we propose APOHA, a theory in which forgetting is not the disposal of knowledge but the operator by which value is learned: the value of a retained item is the counterfactual cost of forgetting it, a learning system is the residue of maximal forgetting subject to preserved value, and higher-order value is the structure that survives repeated forgetting (a renormalisation-relevant invariant), with consolidation as its conjugate. We state the central open problem (a non-trivial attractor with a spectral gap) and test the forgetting theory: operationalising APOHA as an agent on a non-stationary obesity-treatment decision world over 30 seeds, adaptive forgetting cut cumulative decision-regret by 24-32% against never-forget and a fixed half-life, kept a ~6x smaller, cleaner memory, and converged stably; notably, blind forgetting was worse than never forgetting, so the benefit is specific to value-aware forgetting. A multi-disciplinary critique stress-tests the whole.

title: A case-based methodology for computational support of professional ethics evaluation
abstract: Professional fields encode their ethical norms in codes of conduct and accumulate bodies of adjudicated cases that practitioners treat as precedent. Analyzing a new case against that precedent calls for attention to roles, obligations, actions, and the temporal order of events, the same features a review board weighs. ProEthica (proethica.org) demonstrates a transferable five-part methodology for domain-specific ethical case analysis, comprising a nine-component case representation, a three-layer formal ontology, a three-step ontology-constrained extraction process that applies large language models under that ontology, a synthesis step that produces linked analytical views, and a human review loop that governs the shared vocabulary. Two studies evaluate the implementation. The first shows that retrieval over the component-aware representation recovers the precedents expert boards actually cited at higher rates than a section-text embedding baseline. The second finds that engineering-trained evaluators judge each of the five synthesis views helpful for case analysis. The result is a transferable method for converting published ethics opinions into structured, queryable cases that serve both automated precedent retrieval and human deliberation.

title: A Case-Bundle Operating Model for Coding Agents in OpenFOAM-Based CFD
abstract: General-purpose coding agents can set up computational fluid dynamics (CFD) cases, execute solvers, and manage remote jobs. Reviewable and reusable work additionally depends on persistent engineering context and evidence. We present a case-bundle operating model with two modes. Build supports agent-assisted case development under engineering review. Replay applies a reviewed case to new variants. We used this model in an OpenFOAM-7 interFoam study for screening injector designs. GPT-5.5 in Codex helped develop a case bundle containing the simulation configuration, geometry-processing and meshing procedures, remote-execution scripts, post-processing code, and review records. The bundle was replayed to execute and post-process 140 Stereolithography (STL) geometry variants on a remote high-performance computing system. A separate replay exercise used the Pi coding agent as the runtime with four different LLM backends. All four runs succeeded and produced verified results. Tool use and token consumption varied across runs. The results show how reviewed case bundles can support bounded, reusable automation with distinct roles for routine execution and engineering judgment.

title: A Categorial and Sheaf-Theoretic Semantics for Autonomic Component Ensembles
abstract: The proliferation of large-scale, decentralized systems of autonomous agents, such as swarms of robots and networked cyber-physical systems, presents a formidable challenge to traditional formal methods. The Software Component Ensemble Language (SCEL) offers a formal model for such systems, but its operational semantics is not ideal for reasoning about global, structural, and emergent properties. This report proposes a new, multi-layered mathematical model for SCEL using category theory and sheaf theory. We argue that a society of robots described in SCEL can be formally modeled as a sheaf on a topological space, where components are points, ensembles are open sets, and distributed knowledge forms the sheaf's data. In this framework, computational processes like information sharing become equivalent to the sheaf-theoretic operation of "gluing" local data. System failures can then be understood and quantified as topological obstructions, measurable by sheaf cohomology. This approach transforms the verification of a complex distributed system into the analysis of the geometry of a mathematical object, providing deep, structural insights for the design of robust autonomic systems.

title: A Causal Perspective for Enhancing Jailbreak Attack and Defense
venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
abstract: Uncovering the mechanisms behind "jailbreaks" in large language models (LLMs) is crucial for enhancing their safety and reliability, yet these mechanisms remain poorly understood.Existing studies predominantly analyze jailbreak prompts by probing latent representations, often overlooking the causal relationships between interpretable prompt features and jailbreak occurrences.In this work, we propose Causal Analyst, a framework that integrates LLMs into data-driven causal discovery to identify the direct causes of jailbreaks and leverage them for both attack and defense.We introduce a comprehensive dataset comprising 35k jailbreak attempts across seven LLMs, systematically constructed from 100 attack templates and 50 harmful queries, annotated with 37 meticulously designed human-readable prompt features.By jointly training LLM-based prompt encoding and GNN-based causal graph learning, we reconstruct causal pathways linking prompt features to jailbreak responses.Our analysis reveals that specific features, such as "Positive Character" and "Number of Task Steps", act as direct causal drivers of jailbreaks.We demonstrate the practical utility of these insights through two applications: ❶ a Jailbreaking Enhancer that targets identified causal features to significantly boost attack success rates on public benchmarks, and ❷ a Guardrail Advisor that utilizes the learned causal graph to extract true malicious intent from obfuscated queries.Extensive experiments, including baseline comparisons and causal structure validation, confirm the robustness of our causal analysis and its superiority over non-causal approaches.Our results suggest that analyzing jailbreak features from a causal perspective is an effective and interpretable approach for improving LLM reliability.Our code is available at https://github.com/Master-PLC/Causal-Analyst.Warning: Some contents may include disturbing contents.

title: A Causality-Enhanced Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Predictive Maintenance: Taxonomies and Large Language Model-Powered Explanations and Recommendations
A Certified Cost-Sensitive Decision Support Framework for Human Escalation in LLM-Based Intrusion Detection
abstract: Security Operations Centers deploying large language model (LLM)-based intrusion detection face a recurring operational decision: when an alert&apos;s classification should be acted on automatically and when it should be routed to a human analyst. Existing practice relies on ad hoc confidence thresholds or static triage rules that do not connect the decision to its actual operational cost. We present Non-Conformity Score Threshold (NCT), a decision support framework that sets this escalation boundary directly from cost: given a two-stage conformal prediction pipeline (attack detection followed by ATT&CK technique attribution), NCT fits a single operating threshold on a calibration set that minimizes expected cost for a specified miss-to-review cost ratio, using a confidence score computable from model outputs alone at deployment time. Evaluated across 18 model-dataset configurations spanning three benchmark intrusion-detection datasets and six open-weight LLMs (7B-32B parameters), NCT reduces mean operational cost by 83% relative to full automation and 13% relative to ambiguity-triggered escalation (Wilcoxon p<0.01), with analyst load varying widely across configurations (median 25%) in proportion to the underlying model&apos;s top-1 error rate. Cross-dataset experiments expose an asymmetric transfer boundary: thresholds fit on one dataset remain useful when applied to an easier deployment domain but need recalibration in the reverse direction, and the cost curve degrades gracefully toward the theoretically predicted breakeven cost ratio. We support this framework with a finite-sample theory that a practitioner can act on directly: a distribution-free certificate bounding NCT&apos;s deployed cost with no model-selection penalty under a protocol that keeps quantile fitting and threshold fitting on disjoint calibration data, a local diagnostic identifying which operating regions are hard to calibrate from limited data, and a total-variation floor quantifying the cost no confidence-based policy can avoid regardless of calibration size. Together these results turn a conformal uncertainty score into an auditable operational decision variable for human-in-the-loop security automation.

title: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Robust Multi-Robot Manipulation
abstract: Multi-robot systems provide the parallelism and redundancy necessary for long-horizon tasks, while Large Language Models (LLMs) offer the reasoning capabilities to decompose these objectives into actionable plans. However, effectively grounding this high-level reasoning in physical multi-robot execution remains an open challenge. Existing LLM-based approaches fall mainly into two categories: Single-robot methods achieve robust contact-rich manipulation but lack the coordination mechanisms required for tasks spanning multiple workspaces. Current multi-robot frameworks focus on high-level planning, often treating manipulation as an idealized primitive that fails to account for real-world execution uncertainties. To address this, we propose a hierarchical closed-loop agentic LLM-based framework to ensure robust multi-robot manipulation. Our system consists of three specialized agents: the Planning Agent decomposes instructions into allocated sub-tasks, the Manipulation Agent for each robot executes actions via adaptive tool use, and the Verification Agent closes the loop by monitoring physical outcomes and feeding back semantic corrections. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves superior success rates, ensures robust adaptability ranging from single to cross workspace manipulation, and offers a generalizable approach for diverse manipulation tasks.

title: A Cognitive Digital Twin-based Framework for Human-Robot Collaborative Disassembly Integrating Large Language Models
abstract: The field of human-robot collaborative disassembly is plagued by challenges such as data scarcity and limited model generalization, which hinder its efficiency and development in practice. Digital twin (DT) offers a promising solution to these issues. However, DT in collaborative disassembly is impeded by some limitations: it lacks intelligence and cognitive capabilities for the disassembly process, along with a lack of cognitive human modeling. To address this, a cognitive digital twin-based framework for human-robot collaborative disassembly that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) is proposed. The framework comprises three parts: (1) the collaborative robot and human digital twins; (2) a cognitive model constructed based on LLMs, which dynamically generates human disassembly actions by taking disassembly tasks and simulates disassembly behaviors during the disassembly process; (3) virtual generation of human-robot collaborative disassembly data in the twin space, which is applied to optimize the disassembly process. This work constructs a human muscle model to achieve accurate physical modeling, thereby enhancing the realism of the virtual environment. Meanwhile, the integration of LLMs improves the autonomous capability of DT in disassembly task planning. A case study on the disassembly of electric-vehicle batteries is conducted to validate the proposed framework and methods. The results demonstrate that the cognitive digital twin-based modeling framework for human-robot collaborative disassembly supports optimization methods, while reducing data dependence and enhancing model robustness.

title: A collaborative and sustainable engineering design framework enabled by agentic AI
abstract: This study introduces an agentic-AI-enabled S5 collaborative framework for sustainable engineering design that integrates five concurrent dimensions: Sensing, Smart, Sustainability, Social, and Safe within a unified virtual environment. The framework employs agentic AI to coordinate optimisation, risk assessment, and environmental performance in real time, enhancing traceability, transparency, and informed decision-making across digital and physical domains. A case study of a mobile robot for greenhouse operations demonstrates the implementation and lifecycle traceability of the framework. Each agent performs domain-specific optimisation: the Sensing agent ensures perception accuracy and simulation fidelity, the Smart agent reduces path length and energy consumption, the Sustainability agent evaluates life cycle indicators aligned with circular economy principles, the Social agent enables human-AI co-design through immersive visualisation, and the Safe agent validates operational reliability through continuous monitoring. Quantitative results show a 15% reduction in total mass, 12% improvement in energy efficiency, 16.7% increase in recyclability, 92% task validation rate, and a 25% decrease in failure occurrence. These outcomes demonstrate that the S5 framework provides a traceable, data-driven, and human-centric methodology that unifies sustainability, intelligence, and safety. Its modular and scalable architecture supports adoption across domains, such as smart manufacturing, logistics robotics, and sustainable infrastructure.

title: A collaborative approach based on large language model and knowledge graphs for information integration towards smart manufacturing
A Companion Robot Platform for Exploring Technical and Ethical Aspects in Elderly Care
abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are driving significant advancements across various sectors. Combined with robotics, they can lay the foundation for a new paradigm in healthcare, particularly in elderly care and companionship. For years, research has focused on the concept of carebots and robot companions. The latest capabilities of LLMs and robotics promise to address many challenges regarding interaction and personalized experience faced by earlier generations of companion robots. However, the potential of these emerging technologies is accompanied by significant ethical, technical, and social challenges. This chapter presents the design of an elderly care robot that exploits the capabilities of the latest generation of LLMs and considers the ethical, technical, and social implications for improving human-robot interaction capabilities. We report the technical design of a novel robotic platform for elderly care, detailing the devised interaction scenarios, a prototype implementation with NAO and PEPPER robots, and the results of a technical validation that shows the efficiency and feasibility of our system. This study serves as a guide to identify future needs, explore the impact of companion robots on older adults, and understand acceptance of these new approaches.

title: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models for Industrial Cyber-Physical Security
abstract: Intrusion detection in industrial cyber-physical systems is constrained by small labelled-attack corpora and by the subtler signal of physical-process attacks compared with classical IT-network intrusions, motivating renewed interest in foundation-model-based detectors; classical detectors are typically trained per dataset and degrade under the distribution shift that is common in operational technology, where attack repertoires evolve faster than retraining cycles. Two foundation-model families are now plausible candidates: open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) and recent tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabICL) pre-trained for in-context tabular inference. We compare the two families head-to-head, alongside Random Forest and XGBoost classical anchors, across three established industrial security benchmarks (SWaT, HAI, WUSTL-IIoT-2021) under a controlled multi-seed full-holdout protocol with paired McNemar and cross-seed Mann–Whitney tests. The empirical picture is dataset-dependent rather than universal: tabular foundation models establish a strong, previously unreported baseline that is competitive with or superior to classical anchors on every dataset evaluated, while LLMs are complementary detectors with a specific advantage on schemas that carry process-engineering semantics (such as SWaT’s named sensor channels). A per-class analysis on the WUSTL five-class attack taxonomy shows that the two families have structurally different strengths: tabular methods dominate traffic-rich attacks (Denial-of-Service, Reconnaissance), whereas LLMs are competitive on rare attack types (Backdoor, Command Injection). A confidence-gated cascade that escalates only low-confidence tabular decisions to an LLM exceeds either detector alone at a small query budget, and a leave-one-attack-type-out analysis shows that foundation-model detectors generalise to unseen attack families substantially better than the classical anchors. The appropriate detector choice in industrial cyber-physical security is therefore informed by the dataset’s feature schema, the attack-type mix, and the operational cost envelope, rather than by a specific performance metric.

title: A Comparison of Human Capabilities and Large Language Models for Knowledge Representation with Ontologies of Non-Destructive Testing in Bridge Engineering
abstract: Bridge structures are considered complex and significant. Accordingly, the knowledge of the engineering domain of bridge construction and related specialist areas is multidimensional and highly specific. Sometimes this knowledge is explicitly documented in standards, technical regulations, or information sheets. At other times, it resides implicitly in the expertise of the specialists involved. Ontologies are used to structure and formalize such domain knowledge, but creating them is resource-intensive and requires specialized expertise. Large language models (LLMs) offer one way to automate ontology creation through their natural language processing capabilities. This article examines LLMs’ ability to generate ontologies in the specialized field of structural non-destructive testing (NDT) in bridge construction. Four different LLM-based approaches are employed. The results are compared with a previously created human-generated ontology and subsequently evaluated by external experts. Experts rate the human-developed SODIA ontology highest, with an average score of 3.44 out of 5 points. Only the ChatGPT 4.0-created ontology performed similarly well, with a score of 3.3 out of 5.00. All other LLM-based ontologies with ratings below 3.0 are of minor quality. These results underscore the potential and constraints of using LLMs to structure and formalize engineering domain knowledge into ontologies.

title: A Comparison of Human Capabilities and Large Language Models for Knowledge Representation with Ontologies of Non-Destructive Testing in Bridge Engineering
A Comprehensive Review of Generative Physical Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The integration of large-scale foundation models with physical embodiments has led to significant advancements in robotics termed Generative Physical Artificial Intelligence (GPAI). These agentic AI systems autonomously perceive, reason, and act in complex real-world situations. This survey comprehensively analyzes GPAI systems, focusing on their architectural foundations, current applications, and key limitations. We introduce a taxonomy of five distinct approaches: Robot Foundation Models (RFMs) for cross-platform skill transfer; Vision Language Action Models (VLAs) for end-to-end multi-modal perception and control; Large Behavior Models (LBMs) for human-like movement generation; Diffusion Policy Models (DPMs) for diffusion model-based temporally coherent action generation; and World Foundation Models (WFMs) for physics-compliant simulation and data generation. We examine how these approaches complement each other: WFMs generate training data for VLAs and DPMs, RFMs enable cross-platform deployment of learned policies, while LBMs provide motion priors for natural behavior. Through examples across autonomous vehicles, industrial automation, healthcare robotics, and humanoid systems, we identify significant performance improvements and summarize promising research directions in data-efficient learning, sim-to-real transfer, edge-compatible architectures, and safety frameworks. These insights advance embodied AI for IoT-connected environments where intelligent agents interact with networked sensors, actuators, and edge devices.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Large Language Models and Agentic AI Systems for Chemistry and Materials Science
abstract: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has catalyzed a paradigm shift in computational chemistry and materials science, evolving from passive prediction tools to active autonomous agents capable of orchestrating complex scientific workflows. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of LLM based systems in chemistry and materials science from 2020 onwards, establishing a taxonomy that progresses from domain specific language models through tool augmented systems to fully autonomous closed loop discovery platforms. We systematically examine chemical foundation models including ChemBERTa, MoLFormer, and MolT5, alongside materials-focused architecture such as MatSciBERT and MatterGPT. We evaluate their capabilities across molecular property prediction, reaction planning, materials design, and experimental optimization. The review critically analyzes agentic systems such as ChemCrow, Coscientist, and multi agent frameworks that integrate retrieval, simulation tools, and robotic laboratory interfaces to enable autonomous experimentation. Detailed benchmark mappings, evaluation metrics, and reproducibility standards are presented while addressing critical challenges in verification, safety, and trustworthiness for lab facing AI agents. Special emphasis is placed on grounding strategies to mitigate hallucinations, formal constraint validation, and human in the loop safeguards. Our analysis reveals that while current systems demonstrate impressive capabilities in constrained tasks, fundamental challenges remain in true chemical reasoning, uncertainty quantification, and long horizon planning. We conclude by outlining a research agenda for multimodal scientific foundation models, standardized community benchmarks, and governance frameworks necessary for the responsible deployment of autonomous discovery systems in chemistry and materials laboratories.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Physical Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The integration of large-scale foundation models with physical embodiments has led to significant advancements in robotics termed Generative Physical Artificial Intelligence (GPAI). These agentic AI systems autonomously perceive, reason, and act in complex real-world situations. This survey comprehensively analyzes GPAI systems, focusing on their architectural foundations, current applications, and key limitations. We introduce a taxonomy of five distinct approaches: Robot Foundation Models (RFMs) for cross-platform skill transfer; Vision Language Action Models (VLAs) for end-to-end multimodal perception and control; Large Behavior Models (LBMs) for human-like movement generation; Diffusion Policy Models (DPMs) for diffusion model-based temporally coherent action generation; and World Foundation Models (WFMs) for physicscompliant simulation and data generation. We examine how these approaches complement each other: WFMs generate training data for VLAs and DPMs, RFMs enable cross-platform deployment of learned policies, while LBMs provide motion priors for natural behavior. Through examples across autonomous vehicles, industrial automation, healthcare robotics, and humanoid systems, we identify significant performance improvements and summarize promising research directions in data-efficient learning, sim-to-real transfer, edge-compatible architectures, and safety frameworks. These insights advance embodied AI for IoTconnected environments where intelligent agents interact with networked sensors, actuators, and edge devices.

title: A Comprehensive Review on Generative and Parametric Approaches in Cloud – Based CAD/CAM Platforms for 3D Printing Applications
abstract: The integration of parametric and generative design approaches into cloud-based computer-aided design (CAD) and computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) platforms is transforming contemporary product development, especially in 3D printing applications.Parametric design prioritizes constraint-driven, feature-based modelling that embodies designer intent, facilitating editable, reusable, and changeable CAD models.Advanced datasets like WHUCAD, which include attributes such as fillets, chamfers, grooves, and shells, enhance deep learning and replication of human-computer interaction for 3D form development.Prominent parametric cloud systems, like Onshape, Autodesk Fusion 360, Siemens NX, and PTC Creo+, utilize server-side kernels and APIs to provide real-time collaboration and feature mapping.In contrast, generative design utilizes artificial intelligence and algorithmic methods -such as topology optimization, implicit modelling, and large language model (LLM)-assisted script generation -to independently investigate extensive design spaces and enhance products for performance, weight, and manufacturability.Innovative pipelines like ZOO textto-CAD and GPT-enhanced FreeCAD scripting exemplify this approach.Parametric processes thrive in customization and precise assembly control, whereas generative approaches facilitate structural optimization and innovation from exploration, especially when combined with additive manufacturing.Future hybrid design methodologies seek to integrate parametric accuracy with generative creativity; however, obstacles persist in geometric fidelity, computing requirements and manufacturability verification.This study provides a thorough examination of parametric and generative design processes for 3D printing applications, evaluating their techniques, industrial uses, benefits, problems and future potential.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Generative AI: Applications and Future Directions Across Domains
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has become a foundational paradigm for learning complex data distributions and synthesizing realistic content across text, image, audio, tabular, scientific, and multimodal data. Despite rapid progress, the literature remains fragmented across model families and application domains, making it difficult to compare methodological choices, evaluation practices, and domain-specific deployment constraints. This survey addresses this gap by reviewing GenAI from both an algorithmic and cross-domain perspective. Following a PRISMA-inspired search and screening procedure, we organize representative and technically relevant studies across major GenAI families, including variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, diffusion models, autoregressive models, flow-based models, and recent foundation and multimodal models. We synthesize applications across healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing, transportation, earth and environmental systems, computer science and networks, materials science, finance and economics, education, business and services, and creative industries. The review shows that diffusion and autoregressive foundation models increasingly dominate high-fidelity image, language, and multimodal generation, while GANs, VAEs, and flow-based models remain important in data-limited, structured, scientific, and privacy-aware settings. Beyond summarizing applications, the paper compares domain-specific data structures, evaluation practices, robustness concerns, failure modes, and ethical risks. The survey contributes a unified reviewed abstraction of GenAI workflows, a comparison with prior surveys, a domain-aware synthesis of open gaps, and a future roadmap for trustworthy, validated, and responsible GenAI deployment.

title: A Conceptual Framework for ISO/IEC 27001 Audit Augmentation Using Multi-Modal Machine Learning: Integrating Document Review, Field Observation, and Conversational AI Interview
abstract: The audit of Information Security Management Systems (ISMS) under ISO/IEC 27001:2022 has traditionally relied on human auditors whose competence, experience, and judgment shape audit outcomes. While effective, this human-centric approach suffers from inter-auditor variability, high cost, scheduling constraints, and limited scalability — challenges magnified by the post-pandemic shift toward remote audits and the growing volume of organisations seeking certification. Recent advances in Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computer Vision (CV), and Large Language Models (LLMs) suggest that significant portions of the audit workflow could be augmented by machine learning. However, prior research has examined these technologies in isolation; no integrated conceptual framework yet exists that unifies document review, field observation, and interviewing under a single multi-modal pipeline tailored to ISO/IEC 27001 audits and explicitly grounded in the audit methodology of ISO 19011:2018. This paper proposes such a framework — the Multi-Modal ML-Augmented ISO 27001 Audit Framework (M³A-Framework). We synthesise insights from ISO 19011:2018 audit guidelines, recent advances in AI-driven assurance, and the design science research paradigm to develop a five-stage conceptual model that augments the seven-step evidence-collection process specified in ISO 19011 Clause 6.4.7 and that extends the audit-methods matrix of ISO 19011 Annex A (Table A.1). The framework comprises: (1) audit planning and scoping; (2) multi-modal evidence collection through NLP for document analysis, CV for physical control verification (supported by inspection robots and drones), and LLM-based conversational AI for interview; (3) ML-based evidence processing and triangulation; (4) confidence-weighted finding classification using Explainable AI; and (5) human-in-the-loop validation. The framework explicitly maps each module to the 93 controls of Annex A of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and to the audit phases mandated by ISO 19011. We further propose a set of testable propositions, evaluation metrics, and ethical considerations that ground the framework in both academic rigour and practical deployability.

title: A conceptual framework for machine vision integration in manufacturing SMEs
abstract: Abstract Machine vision enables automated quality control, process monitoring, and robotic operations in manufacturing. While adoption is increasing, small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) often face barriers such as limited resources, lack of technical expertise, and standards that do not address their specific needs. This research develops a conceptual framework for SME-oriented machine vision integration. Key requirements were identified through a systematic literature review and expert interviews. A morphological matrix maps these requirements against existing standards and research, forming the basis of a UML-modeled framework. The framework is implemented as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, enabling structured information retrieval via generative AI tools. Validation via a focus group highlighted the framework’s usability, relevance, and coverage. Results provide a foundation for supporting SMEs in adopting machine vision and point to future research opportunities, particularly in enhancing generative AI for interactive automation.

title: A Containerized Multimodal Architecture for On-Device Driver-State Feedback with ROS 2 and Edge AI Services
abstract: Modern automated-driving platforms increasingly rely on multimodal driver monitoring to support supervision and adaptive interaction. However, real-vehicle deployment is often hindered by dependency coupling across robotics middle-ware, sensor drivers, and heterogeneous artificial-intelligence runtimes. We validated an on-device, containerized driver-state feedback architecture that combines Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) acquisition with ROS-free inference containers via a shared-memory (SHM) Bridge, distilling multi-camera video and wearable physiology into compact semantic messages. Vision pipelines were evaluated across heterogeneous runtimes (OpenVINO for head pose, YOLOv8 via ONNX Runtime for person/proximity, and Ultralytics YOLOv8 for driver–object interaction), together with a physiological awareness module. The loop was closed with a local large language model (LLM), served via Ollama (Llama 3.2), to generate structured on-screen and audio feedback. In a one-hour sustained benchmark, the SHM-Bridge overhead averaged 2.45 ms (median 0.21 ms), remaining small relative to inference latency (5.23 ms physiology, 39.26 ms OpenVINO, 189.40 ms ONNX, 313.74 ms Ultralytics, and 2093.05 ms LLM). These results support SHM-Bridge decoupling as a practical strategy for modular multimodal driver monitoring in real vehicles by isolating software dependencies and mitigating runtime conflicts.

This update establishes full engineering closure across physical mechanisms, optical control systems, and high-dimensional instruction orchestration, enabling stable, scalable, and repeatable operation for real-world AGI and LLM workloads. Key architectural advancements include: - All-Cold Dual-Wavelength Pumping A shift to cold-write and cold-erase optical excitation eliminates thermal stress, material damage, and structural drift associated with conventional femtosecond laser processing, enabling sub-micron positional stability and long-term volumetric integrity. - Metastable Non-Excitation Invariance A redefined physical principle for non-volatile yet fully erasable photonic state retention, establishing reliable logic-layer behavior without relying on destructive material modification. - Cross-Hybrid 3D Writing Mechanism A unified writing scheme combining high-throughput area-source full-layer deposition and SLM-based high-precision local refinement. title: A Control System, a Dataset, and a Recipe for Making Frozen LLM Agents Learn a Domain
abstract: Production LLM agents are increasingly assembled from a frozen model wrapped in a harness: a prompt template, a tool set, a memory/retrieval layer, a planning strategy, and a verification policy. Two 2026 systems, Meta-Harness (Lee et al., 2026) and HyperAgents (Meta AI, 2026), show that this harness can itself be optimized or even self-rewritten by an agentic proposer -- at the cost of either an expensive code-search loop or unconstrained self-modifying code, neither of which is auditable or usable with a fully black-box model API. We take a narrower, more constrained position: treat the harness as a small, fixed, human-legible action space and learn a policy over it online with classic sample-efficient reinforcement learning (an $ε$-greedy contextual bandit and REINFORCE), scored against a multi-objective reward (task success, verifier score, policy compliance, cost, latency, and an unsupported-claim penalty). We instantiate this control system with DSPy (Khattab et al., 2024) as both the context assembler and the source of the strongest non-adaptive baseline (a DSPy BootstrapFewShot static prompt), and evaluate it across three verifiable task domains -- tool-use workflows, code generation (HumanEval), and multi-hop retrieval QA (HotpotQA) -- and two model providers (a local Ollama model and AWS Bedrock). We release the harness-control-system code, the cross-domain verifiable task suite, the full trajectory/reward-decomposition logs from training, and a provider-agnostic deployment recipe for applying this to a new organization's domain and verification setup.
