title: An explainable question answering system for equipment maintenance with knowledge-enhanced LLM
An Explicit World Model Based on Data-First Ontology: DaoQL Multimodal Storage Validation and Counterfactual Reasoning Evaluation
abstract: Large language models encode world models implicitly in neural weights, which exposes four structural risks in high-precision domains such as medicine and finance: hallucination, frozen knowledge, poor explainability, and poor modifiability. This paper proposes data-first ontology: LLMs are treated as reasoning and language engines, while deterministic knowledge is moved into an explicit multimodal database, DaoQL. We formalize an explicit world model and show that, under rule independence, deterministic evaluation, and fixed conflict resolution, explicit models provide a sufficient condition for composable counterfactual decomposability; implicit models lack atomic read/delta semantics and therefore provide no comparable architectural guarantee. The implemented system focuses on DaoQL's verified storage layer and explicit Eval path, integrating graph, column, vector, and full-text engines within one process. KVCache graph nodes, expert hot updates, and the DaoQL-Agent runtime remain future work. On an embedded same-machine setup, DaoQL reports graph BFS at 1.20 ms, HNSW at 83.1 us, and a Fluent hybrid query at 105.8 us; these results indicate engineering potential but must be interpreted with deployment-shape differences from client-server systems. Exploratory measurements on LDBC SNB SF1 and ANN-Benchmarks further show 34/34 query coverage with interactive-class queries mostly in the sub-millisecond to millisecond range, but only 1.8 QPS overall due to long-tail BI/IC queries; ANN-Benchmarks reaches Recall@10 >= 99% at thousand-level QPS after a bridge-edge protection fix. In a five-domain counterfactual experiment (n = 1250), DaoQL+GPT-4o achieves 94% composable counterfactual decomposability, 49 percentage points above GPT-4o alone. The paper explicitly separates provable structure, preliminary empirical evidence, and architectural roadmap claims.

title: An Improved Graph Kolmogorov–Arnold Network Based on Mixture of Experts and Its Application in the Key Variable Prediction of Aero-Engine Casing Manufacturing Process
abstract: Accurate prediction of key variables in aero-engine casing manufacturing is critical for ensuring product quality, yet it remains challenging due to the small-sample nature of production data. To address this soft-sensing problem, this paper proposes an improved graph kolmogorov-arnold network-based on mixture of experts (IGKA-MoE) model. The model synergistically integrates multi-modal fusion, physics-informed data augmentation, and a multi-module collaborative mechanism. First, an Expert Knowledge Graph Construction Block (EKGCB) leverages a large language model to transform textual process descriptions into a structured graph representing variable relationships. An Improved Graph Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (IGKAN) then fuses these relational semantics with structured process data through adaptive graph convolution operations. Second, a Novel Sample Generation Block (NSGB) is designed, which incorporates the expert knowledge graph as physical constraints into a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to mitigate data distortion and generate high-quality synthetic samples. Finally, a multi-module collaborative prediction mechanism, governed by a routing block, is employed to separately model real and synthetic samples, effectively alleviating the data imbalance issue and enhancing generalization. Experimental results on a real-world aero-engine casing dataset demonstrate that the proposed IGKA-MoE model significantly outperforms existing methods across multiple error metrics, validating its efficacy for key variable prediction under small-sample conditions.

title: An Improvement in the UVA CS Curriculum: Introduction to Cyber Security; The Sociotechnical Impact of Generative AI on Digital Authenticity and Trust
abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence becomes more integrated into everyday life, people increasingly rely on AI systems to access information, make decisions, and interpret complex data. However, large language models often lack transparency, making it difficult to understand how responses are generated or to verify their accuracy. In complex environments such as universities, where large networks of people, courses, and research outputs are interconnected, finding relevant information efficiently can also be challenging. My technical project and STS research both address issues of trust, transparency, and accessibility in AI systems. My technical project developed a University of Virginia Graph Retrieval Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) system designed to help students navigate academic resources using a structured knowledge graph. My STS research examined the societal implications of AI generated media, particularly concerning authenticity, misinformation, and declining trust in digital content. Together, these projects explore how engineering solutions can improve trust in AI systems while addressing broader societal risks and ethical concerns. STS Project In my STS research, I examined how AI generated media is reshaping digital communication and creating risks related to misinformation and authenticity. As generative AI models improve, they are increasingly capable of producing realistic images, videos, and voice recordings that are difficult to distinguish from human created content. This raises concerns about fraud, misinformation, and declining trust in online platforms. Voice cloning technologies and AI generated content have already contributed to impersonation scams and misleading information. These developments highlight the need for reliable detection tools and transparency mechanisms to help users evaluate digital content. My research concluded that improving transparency and developing detection systems can reduce misinformation and help maintain trust in digital environments. Technical Project The technical project aimed to produce a prototype Graph Retrieval Augmented Generation system for the University of Virginia designed to help users navigate academic resources. A knowledge graph was constructed containing courses, departments, professors, and their research interests and publications, along with the relationships between them. When a user submits a query, the system retrieves relevant information from the graph and passes it to a large language model to generate a grounded response. A key feature of the system is transparency, as users can view a visual representation of the retrieved graph and node information to better understand how the AI generated its response. The system also incorporates personalization using transcript data and conversation history. Testing demonstrated strong factual accuracy, and user feedback indicated that the system was perceived as helpful and trustworthy. Conclusion Working on both the STS

title: An Industrial Application of a Large Language Model to Enhancing Asset Integrity and Process Safety Management
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality, and Human-Centered Computing
abstract: This research incorporates artificial intelligence (AI) into asset integrity and process safety (AIPS) management, aiming to revolutionize conventional methods. It facilitates the automation of risk assessments, enhances predictive analytics, and supports the development of proactive measures to mitigate potential incidents. It explores the application of a generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) based large language models (LLM) to analyse and classify AIPS indicators from vast datasets to generate actionable recommendations to prevent future incidents. A comparative study between two onshore liquefied natural gas (LNG) plants; one utilizing AI-driven AIPS management and the other relying on manual data analysis is presented. The results indicate that AI-driven approaches significantly enhance the accuracy and speed of incident classifications, reducing data processing times. The test model effectively predicts potential future failures by analysing past incident patterns, enabling informed decision-making to prevent and mitigate future failures. The findings highlight the importance of adopting AI-driven AIPS management as a standard practice. It also emphasises the need for stronger collaboration between academia and industry in AI solutions to drive technological advancements for sustainability.

title: An Integrated Ethical and Governance Framework for Agentic Artificial Intelligence Systems
venue: International Journal of Computational and Electronic Aspects in Engineering
abstract: The current state of Agentic Artificial Intelligence which includes AI systems results from two essential technological advancements: machine learning development and large language model technology creation.Agentic AI systems use their system operations to produce decisions which they derive from their environmental analysis.The systems enable users to complete their tasks because they deliver external resources while users maintain their capability to work without needing to operate the system.Organizations which use Agentic AI across healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and digital governance will experience substantial benefits, but they must handle multiple upcoming obstacles.The system operates autonomously which results in two distinct system errors that create unexpected system behavior.Existing AI system regulations fail to control original AI systems because they do not extend their authority to systems that develop intelligence through their operational processes.The research evaluates agentic AI development through its two main themes which lead to essential ethical and governance questions, while showing that existing regulatory frameworks do not effectively resolve these important problems.The paper recommends that organizations require enhanced governance frameworks which include ongoing system assessment and establishment of precise operational standards and human monitoring to protect their systems from potential risks.

title: An Integrated Observability Intelligence Framework: Bridging Semantic Data Modeling, Caching, and LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Root Cause Analysis
abstract: Abstract Modern cloud-native systems generate heterogeneous observability data at unprecedented scale, yet two critical gaps persist in operational intelligence. First, distributed analytical consumers independently reconstruct metric definitions from physical storage schemas, producing inconsistent results across dashboards, pipelines, and LLM-based incident analysis systems. Second, automated root cause analysis frameworks lack a governed, semantically coherent data foundation, causing diagnostic drift when agents query the same metric through divergent pipelines. This paper presents the Integrated Observability Intelligence Framework (IOIF), a unified architecture that couples a Python-native semantic layer with a hierarchical multiagent Large Language Model (LLM) orchestration system. The semantic layer enforces metric consistency through breadth-first search (BFS) join resolution, time-to-live (TTL)-governed caching with portable logical cache keys, and row-level security (RLS) enforcement at the model boundary. Three integration mechanisms bridge the layers: Semantic Context Injection (SCI), Portable Cache Key Propagation (PCKP), and Security Context Threading (SCT). Experimental evaluation on production-scale observability workloads across 350 systematically injected failure scenarios demonstrates a 23.4% reduction in false positive diagnoses and a 31.2% improvement in investigation consistency relative to frameworks operating on ungoverned raw metrics, with a mean time-to-diagnosis of 7.8 minutes.

title: An Integrated Product Service System Framework for On-Site Digital Human Guide Systems
abstract: On-site digital human guide systems, which integrate intelligent interactive technologies with guidance, interpretation, and information services, are emerging as an important form of intelligent on-site service. However, existing knowledge remains largely fragmented across technological configurations, interaction modalities, application contexts, and user experience objectives, lacking an integrated cross-dimensional analytical perspective that explains how these systems create and deliver value. To address this gap, this paper aims to adopt a Product–Service Systems (PSS) perspective to systematically examine the development of on-site digital human guide systems. Specifically, it explores their product–service configurations, service delivery modes and user participation, and artificial intelligence (AI) capability integration pathways, while identifying the value creation opportunities and challenges associated with system development and continuous optimization. The PSS paradigm offers such an integrative lens, which has gained renewed relevance as the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0) accelerates the servitization and digital transformation of traditional services. This paper conducts a scoping review employing content analysis based on a structured cross-database search across Google Scholar, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by snowball sampling, covering 40 studies, including 34 deployed projects. The findings reveal that: (1) on-site digital human guide systems can be categorized into four product–service configurations: fixed terminal (stationary dialogue); mobile terminal (location-aware guidance); Head-Mounted Display/Mixed Reality (immersive experience); and robot (full-process mobile service). The selection of these configurations is shaped by spatial characteristics, target user group, and institutional operational conditions; (2) a user behavior taxonomy of nine active and five passive types was developed, demonstrating that user participation patterns are jointly shaped by control allocation in service delivery and the social behavior design of digital humans, with users showing a preference for controllable and interruptible engagement; (3) AI integration has evolved from rule-and-script-driven approaches to modular AI integration, and subsequently to large language model (LLM)/Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-driven architectures, with corresponding design implications proposed; and (4) challenges were classified into four major categories and 26 subcategories across three digital transformation stages. The contribution of this paper lies in the development of an integrated PSS analytical framework for on-site digital human guide systems, spanning product, service, and AI integration layers. The framework provides a multi-layer analytical lens for understanding system configurations, user participation, technological evolution, and implementation challenges, while offering structured guidance for configur

title: An intelligent automation framework for optimizing purchase invoice processing
abstract: The vast majority of processing of purchase invoices still occurs manually; on average, it costs $9.87 per invoice and can take 12–18 days, as well as having an estimated 12–15 percent error rate. Organizations lack systematic guidance for implementing intelligent automation solutions. This study employed a design science research (DSR) approach to design an integrated, technology-independent framework that incorporates Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies–Intelligent Document Processing (IDP), Large Language Models (LLMs), and Machine Learning (ML) with traditional automation–Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and Robotic Process Automation (RPA). The integrated framework includes five loosely coupled layers: invoice ingestion, document understanding and extraction, validation and business logic, human-in-the-loop decision-making, and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system integration. It also includes technology selection matrices that enable organizations to identify optimal methods for extracting data from their suppliers based on characteristics of their supplier portfolios and value-stratified confidence thresholds to operationalize the degree of risk-appropriate human oversight. Evaluation of the framework using scenarios in both manufacturing and non-profit health care settings demonstrated a potential 50-56% reduction in total cost, a 40-56% improvement in cycle times, and a 70-80% reduction in error rates with a 12-18 month payback period. The framework extends technology acceptance model (TAM) through trust calibration constructs, operationalizes hybrid intelligence theory via confidence-based task allocation, and demonstrates viability for resource-constrained organizations through LLM zero-shot learning and file-based legacy ERP integration.

title: An Intelligent LLM–Fuzzy Decision Support and Digital Twin Framework for Adaptive Agricultural Robotics Systems
abstract: This study develops an integrated LLM–fuzzy decision-support and digital twin framework for adaptive agricultural robotics, combining semantic reasoning, fuzzy inference, multi-objective optimization, and feedback-driven state updating. Numerical sensor data, operational information, and textual field knowledge are transformed into validated decision rules and model-ready parameters, enabling coordinated decisions across economic, operational, crop-stress, and sustainability-related objectives. The framework is evaluated as a simulation-based proof of concept calibrated with real observations from a semi-smart tomato farm, while controlled digital twin scenarios are used to assess its behavior under environmental and operational disturbances. Compared with numerical optimization alone, the complete LLM–fuzzy framework reduces operational cost by 3.35% and crop stress by 7.98%, while improving operational performance by 4.45%. Ablation, repeated-run, scenario, sensitivity, and dynamic-adaptation analyses further demonstrate consistent computational performance under the evaluated conditions. Sustainability is assessed through a model-based measure integrating water use, energy consumption, and soil-compaction-related impacts. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining semantic reasoning, uncertainty processing, optimization, and digital-twin feedback for adaptive agricultural decision support. However, the results represent a calibrated simulation-based proof of concept rather than validation through a full-scale autonomous field deployment; broader multi-season and field-scale validation is therefore required before generalizing the reported operational and sustainability benefits.

title: An Intelligent Q&A System for Production Line O&M Based on Knowledge Graph and GraphRAG
venue: International Conference on Big Data, Information and Computer Network (BDICN)
abstract: In response to the urgent demand for intelligent solutions in production line Operations and Maintenance (O&M), this paper investigates the methodology and workflow for constructing an intelligent Question-Answering (Q&A) system, using a biomass heating production line as a case study. Firstly, O&M knowledge triplets are extracted from technical documents using an improved CasRel-based method, and an O&M Knowledge Graph (KG) is subsequently constructed in the Neo4j graph database. Then, leveraging GraphRAG (Knowledge Graph-Augmented Retrieval Generation) technology, an intelligent Q&A system tailored for the O&M domain of the biomass heating production line is developed. Finally, the system undergoes practical deployment and validation. Experimental results from Q&A application trials demonstrate that the proposed system possesses excellent interactivity and practical utility.

title: An Intelligent Reasoning Framework Based on Multimodal Knowledge Graph for Assembly Planning of Complex Aeronautical Structures
abstract: The functional stability and quality of complex aeronautical structures are directly constrained by the accuracy and effectiveness of assembly planning. However, efficient assembly planning is restricted by complex physical constraints and rules, including unstructured texts, design assembly relationships embedded within 2D drawings and 3D models, rigorous physical assembly standards, and empirical knowledge derived from accumulated historical cases. Developing an optimal assembly scheme necessitates not only adhering to these constraints but also systematically organizing and reasoning over this fragmented engineering information. To this end, a multimodal Knowledge Graph for Assembly Planning (KGAP) is proposed to systematically organize heterogeneous data and support intelligent reasoning of complex aeronautical structures. A hybrid multi-method approach is constructed to resolve the multimodal data challenge: a hybrid deep learning model is utilized for unstructured text analysis, OpenCV-based image processing pipelines are applied to extract features from 2D drawings, and geometric feature extraction algorithms are employed to parse 3D models. Based on the extracted semantics, a domain ontology is defined to align heterogeneous entities, thereby establishing a unified and visualizable knowledge network. On this basis, a reasoning module is designed that integrates Graph Attention Network (GAT) for modeling assembly dependencies with the TOPSIS method for interpretable ranking, which is used to generate and evaluate feasible assembly sequences. Although full-scale industrial validation has not yet been performed, a qualitative comparison with LLM-based planning paradigms indicates that the proposed framework provides superior determinism, constraint compliance, and reasoning traceability for safety-critical assembly planning.

title: An Intelligent Warehouse Execution Framework Integrating SAP Extended WarehouseManagement, Large Language Models, SAP Business Technology Platform, and Autonomous Mobile Robots
An Interactive GraphRAG Workspace for Reifying, Auditing, and Steering Conversational AI Memories
abstract: Conversational Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely employed in software engineering for code generation, debugging, and architectural design. However, as developers engage in multi-session development tasks, technical knowledge becomes siloed in isolated, linear chat histories. Reusing context across sessions leads to three critical challenges: (1) flat-vector retrieval fails to traverse multi-hop relational dependencies between distant architectural decisions; (2) temporal drift in software packages and APIs results in silent context poisoning when reusing aged dialogue logs; and (3) raw conversation concatenation induces prompt bloat and attention degradation. We present CognitiveCanvas, an interactive tool that transforms conversational AI memories from ephemeral text logs into persistent, manipulable, and audited knowledge objects. \textsc{CognitiveCanvas} integrates: (1) a Hierarchical Semantic Fact-Graph (HSFG) that distills dialogues into Goal, Fact, and Code artifacts, achieving a 92.2\% token reduction while enabling multi-hop GraphRAG traversal; (2) a Continuous Temporal Drift Auditor coupling 60+ regex heuristics with live calendar-anchored LLM verification for 1-click self-correction; and (3) a Spatial-Symbolic Prompt Compiler (SSPC) that translates 2D direct manipulation gestures (Voronoi clustering, node resizing, synthesis edges) directly into structured attention directives

title: An Interactive LLM-Based Simulator for Dementia-Related Activities of Daily Living
venue: IEEE/ACM Conference on Connected Health: Applications, Systems and Engineering Technologies
abstract: Effective dementia caregiving requires training and adaptive communication, but assistive AI and robotics are constrained by a lack of context-rich, privacy-sensitive data on how people living with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) behave during activities of daily living (ADLs). We introduce a web-based simulator that uses a large language model (gpt-5-mini) to generate multi-turn, severity- and care-setting-conditioned patient behaviors during ADL assistance, pairing utterances with lightweight behavioral cues (in parentheses). Users set dementia severity, care setting (and time in setting), and ADL; after each patient turn they rate realism (1-5) with optional critique, then respond as the caregiver via free text or by selecting/editing one of four strategy-scaffolded suggestions (Recognition, Negotiation, Facilitation, Validation). We ran an online formative expert-in-the-loop study (14 dementia-care experts, 18 sessions, 112 rated turns). Simulated behavior was judged moderately to highly plausible, with a typical session length of six turns. Experts wrote custom replies for 54.5 percent of turns; Recognition and Facilitation were the most-used suggested strategies. Thematic analysis of critiques produced a six-category failure-mode taxonomy, revealing recurring breakdowns in ADL grounding and care-setting consistency and guiding prompt/workflow refinements. The simulator and logged interactions enable an evidence-driven refinement loop toward validated patient-caregiver co-simulation and support data collection, caregiver training, and assistive AI and robot policy development.

title: An LLM and Knowledge-Graph Based Escalation Engine for Root-Cause Analysis in Advanced Robotics Systems
An LLM-Assisted Framework for Ontology Construction from UCSY Research Papers
abstract: Knowledge engineering plays an essential role in organizing, structuring, and transforming unstructured information into machine understandable knowledge. Ontologies serve as a foundation for knowledge engineering by providing formal representations of concepts, entities, and semantic relationships within a specific domain. As research papers continues to grow rapidly, universities and research institutions face increasing difficulty in systematically managing scholarly information and extracting meaningful insights from dispersed publications. Motivated by these needs, this study proposes an LLM assisted ontology construction framework designed specifically for UCSY computer science and technology research papers. The framework integrates text preprocessing, lexicon-based and linguistic entity extraction, and transformer based relation extraction to automatically generate ontology instances from research metadata and abstracts. Large Language Models (LLMs) are employed to infer semantic relations among tasks, methods, datasets, metrics, and research findings, producing subject, predicate and object triples in a machine-readable RDF format. The constructed ontology enables advanced SPARQL querying, research trend analysis, and cross-paper knowledge exploration, offering a valuable resource for research students and faculty members. The resulting ontology provides a unified semantic layer that supports information retrieval, research trend exploration, and knowledge discovery. Evaluation across multiple papers demonstrates that the ontology effectively captures structured knowledge and assists in answering competency questions relevant to academic research analysis. The proposed approach highlights the potential of LLM-assisted ontology engineering as a scalable and extensible solution for institutional research knowledge management.

title: An LLM-assisted multi-agent control framework for roll-to-roll manufacturing systems
abstract: Roll-to-roll manufacturing requires precise tension and velocity control to ensure product quality, yet controller commissioning and adaptation remain time-intensive processes dependent on expert knowledge. This paper presents an LLM-assisted multi-agent framework that automates control system design and adaptation for R2R systems while maintaining safety. The framework operates through five phases: system identification from operational data, automated controller selection and tuning, sim-to-real adaptation with safety verification, continuous monitoring with diagnostic capabilities, and periodic model refinement. Experimental validation on a R2R system demonstrates successful tension regulation and velocity tracking under significant model uncertainty, with the framework achieving performance convergence through iterative adaptation. The approach reduces manual tuning effort while providing transparent diagnostic information for maintenance planning, offering a practical pathway for integrating AI-assisted automation in manufacturing control systems.

title: An LLM-based approach to maximize the :effectiveness of Industrial Internet of :Things implementations through the :selection of architecture
abstract: The selection of the most suitable architectural pattern for Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) applications within the Industry 4.0 paradigm presents a critical challenge, as organizations grapple with a variety of contexts, sophisticated architecture, complex deployment, stringent performance requirements, and evolving security concerns. This thesis develops and validates a transparent, LLM-based approach and a decision framework for pattern selection. The approach formalizes decision rules that are used to select appropriate IIoT architecture for a provided use-case. Evidence was assembled through a qualitative synthesis of approximately 5,000 publications that were programmatically collected, deduplicated, ranked for relevance, and mined for key metrics describing pattern attributes and reported contexts. Domain experts in IoT were asked in a survey to subsequently specify use-case descriptions and decide how much weight to give each evaluation criterion, which were predefined. This expert mapping constitutes the ground truth that instantiates the theoretical model within the decision framework. A large language model (LLM) was deployed as a tool for context specialization, transforming generic architectural knowledge into case-specific recommendation. Conditioned on the expert-validated pattern–use-case mapping, the model in-gests previously unseen architecture/use-case descriptions and returns a rank-ordered set of suitable architectural patterns with accompanying rationales. The LLM operationalizes and generalizes expert knowledge to novel contexts. The findings indicate that pattern suitability is highly context specific, and that a structured, data-driven approach significantly enhances decision confidence. By formalizing pattern–usecase mappings and incorporating expert judgments, the research delivers a twofold contribution. On the one hand, it establishes a approach for making sense of IIoT architectural choices. On the other hand, it provides a practical, data-driven approach that system architects can apply immediately. The primary users of this approach are system architects, solution engineers, and industrial IT decision makers in manufacturing and industry related sectors. The secondary users include researchers and lecturers who can employ the model as a teaching and benchmarking instrument. Future studies might look at systems that adjust in real-time and examine their pros and cons across different industrial settings.

title: An LLM-Based Assistance System for Intuitive and Flexible Capability-Based Planning
venue: IEEE International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
abstract: In modern industry, dynamic environments and the complexity of modular and reconfigurable resources require automated planning of process sequences. Capability-based planning approaches address this by automatically generating plans from semantic knowledge models that describe resource functions in a machine-interpretable form. Their practical use, however, remains limited: solver feedback, especially in the case of unsatisfiability, is difficult to interpret, and the knowledge models require adaptation as operational conditions change or requests become infeasible. This paper presents a hybrid assistance system that augments an existing capability-based Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) planning approach with an Large Language Model (LLM)-based layer for natural-language interaction, explanation, and adaptation. Formal planning correctness remains with the symbolic planner, while the LLM layer handles natural-language access and flexible knowledge model adaptation under explicit Human-in-the-Loop (HitL) approval. The system decomposes into four components: Capability Grounding, Symbolic Planning, Result Interpretation, and Planning Adaptation, realized as a routed agentic workflow in which a central router delegates to five specialized agents. The system is evaluated on a modular production system across four scenario types. Of 23 test cases, 9 of 10 knowledge queries and all 4 satisfiable planning cases were handled correctly, 3 of 4 unsatisfiable cases produced concrete repair proposals, and all 5 adaptive planning scenarios resolved into satisfiable plans through iterative, user-approved knowledge model modifications. The findings confirm that combining formal planning with LLM-based assistance substantially improves accessibility and adaptability in industrial automation.

title: AN LLM-BASED DECISION INTEGRATOR WITH STRUCTURED OUTPUT AND A SIX-GATE ANALYTICAL RUBRIC FOR A/B TESTING DECISION SUPPORT
abstract: The statistical layer of a modern experimentation pipeline produces more numbers than decisions, and integrating its dozen signals into one defensible call has remained manual work. The paper proposes a decision integrator built on a large language model constrained twice: structured output against a fixed JSON schema closes the space of recommendations to four labels (ship, do not ship, keep running, investigate), and a six-gate analytical rubric in an immutable versioned system prompt fixes the order in which evidence is weighed, so no later gate can override an earlier one. A deterministic template guarantees a baseline report when the model is unavailable. Over two months of production use all 20 calls returned schema-valid JSON, the recommendation and confidence fields stayed stable across repeated calls on identical inputs, and one call costs about three cents and three to four seconds.

title: An LLM-based multi-agent system for manufacturing decision support: material–process recommendation and process parameter optimization
venue: Proceedings of the MMRL-XMO Industrial Seminar 2026
abstract: As product fabrication environments become increasingly diverse, there is a growing need for decision support that connects users’ fabrication intents and requirements to appropriate manufacturing conditions. In this study, we propose an LLM-based multi-agent system for manufacturing decision support that systematically supports material and process recommendation, equipment selection, process parameter optimization, and result prediction. The proposed system utilizes manufacturing literature and technical documents through RAG-based manufacturing knowledge retrieval and excludes low-relevance documents before response generation by verifying the relevance of retrieved documents to the user query. In addition, it explores support relationships among materials, processes, and equipment based on a knowledge graph and derives process parameters that satisfy the target characteristics using optimization metadata and surrogate models for each combination of process, material, and equipment. To address users’ diverse queries and complex requirements for manufacturing decision support, task-specific agents were defined and organized into two teams: a material and process recommendation team and a process optimization team. These teams were then integrated into a hierarchical multi-agent architecture coordinated by a Supervisor agent. The application results showed that the proposed system can dynamically assign appropriate agents according to the purpose and requirements of user queries, and support manufacturing decision-support tasks by linking unstructured knowledge retrieval, structured relationship exploration, process optimization, and result prediction. These results suggest the potential of the proposed system to support information retrieval, condition evaluation, and optimization in complex manufacturing decision-support workflows.

title: An LLM-based Two-Stage Transformer Framework for Cross-Domain Bearing Fault Diagnosis with Limited Data
venue: IEEE/ASME International Conference on Advanced Intelligent Mechatronics
abstract: Bearing fault diagnosis faces critical challenges when dataset heterogeneity, operating condition variations, and limited labeled data occur simultaneously in industrial environments. Existing approaches address these issues in isolation and rely on implicit feature alignment, limiting effectiveness under concurrent challenges. This paper proposes a knowledge-guided two-stage transfer learning framework that employs a lightweight GPT-2-style Transformer with causal self-attention for hierarchical feature extraction from vibration signals, establishing explicit pathways where pre-trained encoder weights and fault prototype embeddings serve as knowledge carriers from multi-source pre-training to target adaptation. The framework addresses the dual-shift challenge through multi-source learning for generalizable representations, prototype-based knowledge modulation for target adaptation, and taxonomy-adaptive classification for seamless transfer across heterogeneous fault categories. Experimental validation on four real-world datasets demonstrates 92.61% average accuracy with only 10% labeled target data, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by 17.24 percentage points, establishing a practical pathway toward cost-effective predictive maintenance in Industry 4.0 applications.

title: An LLM-Driven Closed-Loop Autonomous Learning Framework for Robots Facing Uncovered Tasks in Open Environments
abstract: Autonomous robots operating in open environments need the ability to continuously handle tasks that are not covered by predefined local methods. However, existing approaches often rely on repeated large-language-model (LLM) interaction for uncovered tasks, and even successful executions or observed successful external behaviors are not always autonomously transformed into reusable local knowledge. In this paper, we propose an LLM-driven closed-loop autonomous learning framework for robots facing uncovered tasks in open environments. The proposed framework first retrieves the local method library to determine whether a reusable solution already exists for the current task or observed event. If no suitable method is found, it triggers an autonomous learning process in which the LLM serves as a high-level reasoning component for task analysis, candidate model selection, data collection planning, and execution or observation strategy organization. The robot then learns from both self-execution and active observation, performs quasi-real-time training and adjustment, and consolidates the validated result into the local method library for future reuse. Through this recurring closed-loop process, the robot gradually converts both execution-derived and observation-derived experience into reusable local capability while reducing future dependence on repeated external LLM interaction. Results show that the proposed framework reduces execution time and LLM dependence in both repeated-task self-execution and observation-driven settings, for example reducing the average total execution time from 7.7772s to 6.7779s and the average number of LLM calls per task from 1.0 to 0.2 in the repeated-task self-execution experiments.

title: An LLM-Driven Framework for Automated Knowledge Graph Construction from Engineering Educational Resources
venue: 2026 International Conference on AI in Education Technology and Applications (AIETA)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of automated Knowledge Graph (KG) construction in “Knowledge-Dense” engineering domains, where traditional methods struggle to reconcile textual concepts with rigid mathematical constraints. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer strong reasoning capabilities, they are prone to “domain hallucination” when linking physical components to their governing formulas. We propose a specialized framework for the “Fundamentals of Mechanical Design” curriculum that moves beyond simple entity extraction. The core contribution is a domain-specific constraint mechanism that enforces engineering logic—ensuring mathematical models are correctly semantically bound to their respective physical entities (e.g., ensuring a “Hertzian Stress” formula is linked to “Gears” rather than “Columns”). Experimental evaluations confirm that this ontology-driven refinement significantly outperforms baseline LLM extraction, specifically in resolving formula-component dependencies. The result is a rigorous, hallucination-resistant knowledge base serves as a necessary foundation for reliable intelligent engineering tutoring.

title: An LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Evolution Framework for Solver Code Generation in Job Shop Scheduling
abstract: Developing high-quality and reliable solver code for the job shop scheduling problem (JSSP) remains a challenging and expertise-intensive task because generated code must stay executable, produce feasible schedules, and achieve strong scheduling results. This paper proposes a large language model (LLM)-driven multi-agent evolution framework for scheduling solver code generation, where LLMs act as hyper-heuristics for program-space search under external evaluation. The framework forms a closed-loop process with three collaborating agents. A seed heuristic generation agent uses a structured constraint template and a shared solver skeleton to synthesize, screen, and diversify seed programs to construct a competitive initial code pool. An evolutionary operator agent updates the pool through program-space crossover and best-so-far mutation. A code reflection agent analyzes solver code and maintains trajectory-aware reflective memory to generate structured guidance for later revision. Experiments on standard JSSP benchmarks show that the framework outperforms representative metaheuristics across heterogeneous instance families and scales while reaching best-known reference quality on a subset of instances. Ablation results further confirm the contributions of the initialization design and the reflection-guided revision mechanism. More broadly, the proposed framework helps reduce manual heuristic design effort and offers a practical approach to production scheduling optimization in intelligent manufacturing environments.

title: An LLM-Driven Visual Automation Script Generation Framework for Mixed-State Testing in Industrial Applications
abstract: Visual automation frameworks have matured considerably in recent years, yet a stubborn challenge persists in industrial practice: the so-called “mixed-state” test cases. These scenarios intertwine explicit user interface (UI) interactions with implicit backend state verifications, creating a semantic chasm that conventional parsing approaches fail to bridge. DOM-reliant tools suffer from selector brittleness and state blindness, while purely visual methods cannot detect underlying data mutations. This paper introduces a Vision-Language Model (VLM)-driven framework that decouples intent comprehension from physical test execution. At its core lies a dual-layer intent classifier combining Sentence-BERT embeddings with Large Language Model (LLM)-based Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, enabling accurate categorization of heterogeneous test steps. For invisible backend mutations, we propose a “Reverse Oracle” causal inference engine that traverses a UI-Data knowledge graph to translate hidden states into observable visual assertions. A weighted multiplicative scoring model coupled with a tri-branch adaptive fallback mechanism ensures robust execution across diverse industrial scenarios. Experiments on 638 real-world test cases demonstrate that our approach elevates mixed-state automation success rates from 29.3% to 90.8%, while reducing average step latency to 1.03 seconds. These results point toward more resilient and maintainable test automation in enterprise environments.

title: An LLM-enhanced knowledge service methodology for manufacturing process planning based on task- guided multi-layer knowledge graph
An LLM-KG Collaborative Traceability Question-Answering System for TWT Manufacturing
abstract: Traveling-wave tube (TWT) manufacturing is characterized by high product variety, low batch volume, and complex process workflows. Under rapid delivery and frequent iteration, typical issues arise, including fragmented information, low query efficiency, and insufficient interaction flexibility. This paper focuses on traceability of key process problems in TWT manufacturing and presents an integrated question-answering (QA) system with deep collaboration between a knowledge graph $(K G)$ and a large language model (LLM). The system integrates natural language processing (NLP) with KG techniques to organize dispersed, unstructured manufacturing knowledge-such as anomalies, causes, simulation reproduction clues, and process stages-into a connected, evidence-chain network. On this basis, an LLMKG collaborative semantic layer is constructed, enhancing the ability to disambiguate restricted entities and complete information in multiple rounds for complex natural language queries, and structuring the retrieval results into evidence-based responses. By limiting the output to KG-hit evidence, this system improves traceability efficiency while maintaining verifiability.

title: An LLM-powered Chatbot for Knowledge Management in Manufacturing Automation
venue: KTH Publication Database DiVA (KTH Royal Institute of Technology)
abstract: Knowledge is a key strategic resource for organizations, and an organization’s ability to successfully manage and transfer knowledge has a wide range of impacts on key performance indicators. This study looked at how Elektroautomatik, a small Swedish automation company could improve their knowledge management process through use of generative AI. Prior to this study employees at Elektroautomatik used a OneNote document (Kunskapsbank) to manage knowledge across various automation projects. This study proposed solution in the form of an LLM-powered chatbot that utilized a Neo4J GraphRAG database built off the Kunskapsbank document. An iterative design and creation process was used to develop the chatbot first utilizing a RAG retrieval model, then a GraphRAG with a monolingual query function for the chatbot, and finally a bilingual query function that could search information in the GraphRAG in both English and Swedish. Developing the RAG and GraphRAG required specialized data generation and query handling processes as the Kunskapsbank document contained a mix of information in a mixed media format of text, images, and tables, and was written in both English and Swedish. The chatbot was evaluated based on a set test questions and ground truths developed by Elektroautomatik using the RAGAS metrics context precision, context recall, semantic similarity, factual correctness, and faithfulness. The three methods, RAG, monolingual GraphRAG query, and bilingual GraphRAG query were all evaluated, and the bilingual GraphRAG query had the best performance overall. Through the development of this LLM-powered chatbot the study was able to demonstrate how generative AI could be used to develop a knowledge management system that could handle a mixed media and bilingual knowledge dataset. Future studies should focus on improving performance of Swedish language queries, evaluating the system on a more robust set of test questions, and following up on user testing evaluation after completing a full application. Additionally, the LLM-powered chatbot knowledge management system developed in this thesis should be tested at other manufacturing automation companies to verify results.

title: An LLM‐Enabled Human–Machine Collaborative Fault Diagnosis Framework via Industrial AI Agents
abstract: ABSTRACT Intelligent fault diagnosis (FD) of mechanical equipment is vital for ensuring the safety and stability of industrial systems. As modern industrial environments continue to expand in scale and complexity, systematic FD increasingly requires not only accurate signal pattern recognition but also flexible human–machine collaboration for task configuration, model selection and decision optimisation. Traditional static diagnostic systems based on small‐scale specialised models (SSMs) are often inadequate for dynamic, multisource and heterogeneous diagnostic tasks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a large language model (LLM)‐enabled human–machine collaborative fault diagnosis framework that combines multimodal task interpretation, signal‐source identification and dynamic selection of registered SSMs. The LLM operates at the task‐cognition level, whereas structured task checking, model applicability validation and human review for uncertain cases prevent uncertain cognitive outputs from directly triggering deterministic diagnosis. Experiments on two public datasets and an industrial spindle‐motor dataset show that the agent achieves 87.33% SSM selection accuracy and 75.00% end‐to‐end diagnosis accuracy without additional labelled samples for training a separate router, outperforming deterministic rule routing. These results indicate a feasible architecture for heterogeneous industrial diagnosis that combines flexible LLM‐based task understanding, deterministic SSM diagnosis and explicit human review for uncertain tasks.

title: An Onto-LLM-based framework for automating construction supervision specification knowledge graph generation
venue: International Conference on Communication, Information, and Digital Technologies (CIDT)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of fragmentation of specification knowledge and insufficient intelligence in management in the field of construction supervision engineering, this study proposes a natural language specification semantic interpretation and knowledge graph automatic construction method based on Ontology-Guided Large Language Model (Onto-LLM). By analyzing the core elements of supervision specifications, a domain ontology model including seven dimensions such as safety management and quality control is constructed, and the ontology is built using the improved seven-step method. Based on the DeepSeek large language model, combined with the collaborative mechanism of few-shot learning and in-context learning, a prompt template integrating domain features and triple constraints is designed to realize semantic interpretation of specification clauses and triple extraction. The extraction accuracy is improved through ontology constraint filtering and relationship consistency verification. Finally, the GraphDB graph database is used to construct the knowledge graph, realizing rapid retrieval and associative analysis of domain knowledge. Taking the interpretation of 200 current construction engineering supervision specification clauses as a verification case, the results show that this method effectively improves the structural degree and semantic relevance of supervision specification knowledge, significantly enhances the efficiency and accuracy of knowledge graph construction, and provides support for intelligent management and application of domain knowledge.

title: An Onto-Relational-Sophic Framework for Governing Synthetic Minds
abstract: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence, from task-specific systems to foundation models exhibiting broad, flexible competence across reasoning, creative synthesis, and social interaction, has outpaced the conceptual and governance frameworks designed to manage it. Current regulatory paradigms, anchored in a tool-centric worldview, address algorithmic bias and transparency but leave unanswered foundational questions about what increasingly capable synthetic minds are, how societies should relate to them, and the normative principles that should guide their development. Here we introduce the Onto-Relational-Sophic (ORS) framework, grounded in Cyberism philosophy, which offers integrated answers to these challenges through three pillars: (1) a Cyber-Physical-Social-Thinking (CPST) ontology that defines the mode of being for synthetic minds as irreducibly multi-dimensional rather than purely computational; (2) a graded spectrum of digital personhood providing a pragmatic relational taxonomy beyond binary person-or-tool classifications; and (3) Cybersophy, a wisdom-oriented axiology synthesizing virtue ethics, consequentialism, and relational approaches to guide governance. We apply the framework to emergent scenarios including autonomous research agents, AI-mediated healthcare, and agentic AI ecosystems, demonstrating its capacity to generate proportionate, adaptive governance recommendations. The ORS framework charts a path from narrow technical alignment toward comprehensive philosophical foundations for the synthetic minds already among us.

title: An Ontology-Aware Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Competency Extraction and Knowledge Graph Maintenance in Engineering Education
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Competency-based education depends on a structured representation of knowledge, skills, learning outcomes, and prerequisite relationships. The main research question addressed in this paper is: Can an LLM-based agent reliably extract, align, and maintain competency knowledge from unstructured educational documents while preserving ontology consistency, traceability, and human feedback? This paper presents CORE (Competency Ontology RAG Engine), an ontology-aware human-in-the-loop AI agent designed to automate competency ontology maintenance while preserving accuracy and traceability. We designed a core that is an ontology-aware RAG engine based on a competency ontology and integrated human validation in the loop. It has a basic five-step procedure in which orchestration is done by LangGraph. We extract text from source documents, while RDF and OWL deal with ontology alignment. This updated knowledge graph is stored in Neo4j. In the end, Semantic MediaWiki introduces the field specialists to evaluate, revise, and approve the knowledge generated by the agent. We built a prototype to test this approach. This agent performed ontology alignment 95% accurately, showed 8 competency entities at 80% average confidence, and showed 85% embedding. Neo4j stored 100 nodes for competency entities while it detected 100 human edits on the feedback loop. This makes the whole pipeline more efficient and reliable for maintenance of AI-based competency ontology in education engineering knowledge graphs.

title: An ontology-driven bayesian network approach to fault diagnosis and correction in manufacturing
venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
abstract: Abstract Efficient Fault Diagnosis and Correction (FDC) is crucial for maintaining high availability in manufacturing systems. This paper presents a novel ontology-driven approach for creating Bayesian Networks (BNs) to support decision-making in FDC. An ontology is developed to represent fault knowledge from domain-specific data sources, including Failure Mode, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) data. This ontology is used as a template for creating the BN structure. The probability parameters of the BN are identified heuristically via FMECA criticality information, deterministic relationships, and expert knowledge. A case-based evaluation using an assembly line for solenoid valves demonstrates the BN’s accurate FDC prediction performance.

title: An Ontology-driven MCP Agent Framework for Ensuring Integrity in Architectural Structural Design
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Large Language Model (LLM)-based autonomous agents has demonstrated strong potential for automating knowledge-intensive tasks. However, their probabilistic reasoning often leads to hallucinations and weak domain knowledge integrity, limiting their applicability in high-stakes architecture, engineering, and construction (Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC)) contexts where engineering reliability is critical. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel architecture, termed the Ontology-driven Model Context Protocol (O-MCP) Framework, which integrates formal ontology with the standardized Model Context Protocol to ensure logical consistency and trustworthy knowledge exchange. The framework introduces a three-layer architecture consisting of a Knowledge and Data Source Layer, a Semantic MCP Server Layer, and an Intelligent Agent Layer. Its core contribution is the Semantic MCP Server, which incorporates a semantic guardrail mechanism that validates agent requests in real time using ontology-based reasoning. A case study in architectural structural design illustrates how the framework formalizes expert tacit knowledge and preserves decentralized knowledge sovereignty. A proof-of-concept experiment in reinforced concrete slab design positions O-MCP as a reference standard for formalized expert knowledge. Results show that while LLM-based RAG systems achieve approximately 83% agreement, systematic errors persist in numerical reasoning and multi-condition rule application, highlighting the value of formal ontological verification for guaranteeing engineering integrity.

title: An ontology-guided knowledge-graph and case-based reasoning framework with LLM-assisted extraction for joint resilience-and-sustainability decision support in production networks
abstract: Production networks are now required to withstand disruptions while also meeting rising sustainability expectations. These two requirements interact directly. Redundancy can improve resilience but increase resource use; lean efficiency can reduce waste but weaken operational buffers. Existing tools usually treat the two domains separately, leaving engineers to connect scattered evidence from reports, standards, and case studies manually. This project develops an integrated decision-support system for extracting, structuring, and recommending resilience and sustainability measures from unstructured corporate documents. A source document is ingested as a PDF, URL, or plain-text input; cleaned and chunked; processed through a constrained LLM extraction step; and then checked through deterministic substring verification. A retrieval-augmented ontology-mapping stage, KROMA, narrows the classification space before assigning each accepted measure to one of 19 resilience factors and one of 10 ESRS-aligned sustainability standards. The verified measures and their provenance are stored in a Neo4j knowledge graph with 67 directed influence relationships across three Impact Categories. A case-based reasoning module retrieves related measures from 228 curated ontology entries to support pattern-level recommendation. The system was evaluated across six pipeline runs spanning technology, manufacturing, and aviation documents. Extraction confidence averaged 0.916 to 0.926, verbatim evidence pass rates ranged from 62.5% to 100%, and ontology confirmation rates ranged from 92.3% to 100%. All 26 CBR robustness tests and all 6 adversarial stress tests passed. The internal ablation showed that KROMA improves classification diversity: without it, assignments collapsed into two broad factors; with it, Shannon diversity improved from less than 0.15 to 0.305. The Boeing representative-subset benchmark produced 23 measures with 100% verbatim fidelity and one soft action-verb vocabulary flag. Overall, the project demonstrates a traceable proof-of-concept workflow for joint resilience and sustainability analysis in production networks. Rather than relying on unconstrained generation, the system couples model-assisted extraction with rule-based verification and fixed ontology boundaries, so each accepted measure can be inspected from source evidence to graph record.

title: An open-source reference framework for the implementation of type 3 Asset Administration Shells
abstract: Seamlessly integrating assets into distributed digital ecosystems based on Industry 4.0/5.0 demands measurable impact: lower engineering cost, interoperability and adaptability. SMIA (Self-configurable Manufacturing Industrial Agents) addresses this as an reference framework for implementing autonomous digital counterparts of assets, unifying industrial and software standards. Its dual-layer architecture combines machine-interpretable semantic modeling with distributed functional software, enhancing interoperability, flexibility, and autonomy. SMIA represents assets by executing domain-specific tasks and performing peer-to-peer communication through standardized interfaces. Following open scientific software principles, it integrates mature technologies and provides reproducible deployment artifacts (e.g., Docker), ensuring traceability and extensibility while reducing engineering effort and technological fragmentation. • SMIA is an open-source reference framework that automates AAS type 3 digitization. • It joins standardization efforts from industrial and software engineering fields. • It boosts interoperability, flexibility, and autonomy across heterogeneous systems. • Normalized Digital Twins are self-configured from semantically enriched AAS models. • Built on open scientific software engineering for modularity and extensibility.

title: An Operation‐Trajectory Guided Self-Evolving Reasoning Multimodal LLM Agent for Oxygen Lance Control in BOF Steelmaking
abstract: Oxygen lance control is a critical decision-making task in basic oxygen furnace (BOF) steelmaking. It regulates lance height to control decarburization rate, aiming to achieve stability. Existing approaches either rely on human expertise, requiring long-term training and experience accumulation, or use traditional machine-learning models that simplify the problem into numerical regression, resulting in limited interpretability and adaptability. In this work, we are the first to reformulate oxygen lance control as a structured multimodal generative decision-making task and propose a self-evolving reasoning Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) agent that performs structured reasoning. The agent jointly perceives real-time furnace mouth flame videos and historical process data to generate structured decision paths. To address the scarcity of high-quality annotated industrial data, we introduce OT-SERA, an Operation‐Trajectory guided Self‐Evolving Reasoning MLLM Agent for structured decision-making. OT-SERA includes an initialization phase and a refinement phase. In the Operation-Trajectory Guided Reasoning Initialization (OTGRI) phase: operation trajectories from real BOF steelmaking guide the generation of structured chain-of-thoughts (CoTs), which are then used to warm-up the agent by fine-tuning. In the Self-Evolving Reasoning Refinement (SERR) phase: the agent improves reasoning paths through self-evolving updates with path backtracking, automatically constructing high-quality CoTs without additional human annotation. Repeated the SERR further improve CoTs quality, highlighting the effectiveness. Extensive experiments on real-world BOF data show that OT-SERA outperforms strong time series and multimodal baselines under both normal and hard operating conditions. By integrating multimodal perception, OTGRI, and SERR, this work provides an effective solution for intelligent control of complex industrial processes.

title: An optimized method for retrieval-augmented generation towards multimodal knowledge bases in underground space
venue: International Conference on Computer Graphics, Artificial Intelligence, and Data Processing (ICCAID)
abstract: The technical documents accumulated in the field of underground space engineering represent valuable knowledge assets. However, their multimodal (e.g., text, tables, diagrams) and unstructured nature leads to inefficient knowledge retrieval and utilization. Conventional methods struggle with complex, cross-modal queries, while using large language models (LLMs) directly for answer generation carries the risk of factual hallucinations and contextual incoherence, failing to meet the precision requirements of professional applications. To address these challenges, this study focuses on optimizing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system for underground space. First, we propose a text segmentation method based on document logical structure, which divides text into semantic units according to headings and numbering, establishing a solid foundation for subsequent knowledge extraction. Second, we develop a prompt optimization mechanism with hybrid terminology injection (static glossary + dynamic corpus mining), significantly enhancing the system's ability to identify key entities and relationships. Furthermore, the system integrates a multimodal output function, enabling the generated textual answers to be automatically linked with and presented alongside original charts and diagrams, providing users with intuitive visual evidence. We constructed a domain-specific knowledge graph using a dataset of 300 weekly reports from a project and conducted a systematic evaluation with statistical significance tests. Experimental results confirm that the optimized system significantly outperforms conventional approaches and the unoptimized baseline across multiple metrics (answer faithfulness, relevance, context precision, context recall), with all improvements validated to be statistically significant (p<0.05).

title: An Overview of Knowledge-Based System: History, Advances and Challenges in the Era of Large Language Models
abstract: With 60 years of research, knowledge-based system has travelled a long journey from early small-scale rule-based programs to modern super-large-scale knowledge graphs. Several multithreading technical stages can be broadly categorized: early history of rule-based system, knowledge engineering, semantic network, semantic web, ontology engineering, knowledge graph, and recent advances driven by machine learning. In the past couple years, the whole area of artificial intelligence including knowledge-based system has been significantly influenced by large language models, which dramatically increases the understanding and utilization of knowledge by increasing to an extremely large scale. Considering the long-standing intrinsic problems of large language models such as hallucination and lack of explainability, the challenge of how to build reliable large-scale knowledge-based systems in an effective and economical way still exists. From the overview of the developing history, we can see a promising research direction of combining large language models with those traditional knowledge-based frameworks.

title: An Uncertainty-Gated Neuro-Symbolic Framework for High-Coverage Topic Modeling and Trend Analysis in Scholarly Corpora With LLM Assistance
abstract: The rapid growth of scientific literature demands scalable methods that can track research evolution, yet density-based topic models such as BERTopic systematically exclude low-density documents as outliers, obscuring emerging and niche research areas.We propose aNeuro-Symbolic, Uncertainty-Gated Frameworkthat recovers these outliers through geometric centroid reassignment and an ontological entropy gate derived from the Computer Science Ontology (CSO), routing only genuinely ambiguous cases to a local Large Language Model (Qwen2.5-14B via Ollama, temperature=0.0). A controlled ablation study demonstrates that centroid reassignment provides the largest coverage gain (+22.9 percentage points (pp)), the CSO entropy gate preserves niche-topic integrity, and selective LLM routing adds an additional +5.9 pp. On 12,535 Turkish computer engineering theses (2001–2025), the full pipeline raises coverage from 74.6% to 95.4% while maintaining competitive coherence (NPMI=0.100) and stability (AMI=0.832), at ∼15×fewer LLM calls than a fully generative Pure-LLM baseline. Mann–Kendall trend tests on the high-coverage series identify 69 statistically significant trends (FDRq< 0.05), and cross-corpus validation on 200K arXiv CS abstracts confirms that the architecture generalizes beyond the primary dataset. The framework offers a reproducible, cost-effective solution for monitoring scientific developments in rapidly evolving fields.

title: Analysis of Mutual and Referential Human and Robot Gazes in a Collaborative Word Association Game
abstract: Robot gaze is a major component of human-robot dialogue coordination. Most studies of gaze in human-robot dialogue focus on face-to-face social conversations, but little is known about gaze in demanding task-focused interactions. In this paper, we investigate how the gaze of a robot game partner affects human visual attention and if humans tend to direct confirmation-seeking gazes towards the robot. In our study, we let participants play a collaborative word association game with a NAO robot acting as an embodied, LLM-driven conversational partner. Our experiments are conducted under two conditions, which implement mutual and referential gazes of the robot respectively. We record participants' gaze using eye tracking glasses and analyze the interactions using gaze coordinates, speech segments, key events and areas of interests. We find that robot gaze orientation does not affect the time to first fixation on words the robot proposed. We also find that participants gaze more often at the robot when their dialogue line contains confirmation requests, compared to when it does not. Our results indicate (likely also due to the cognitively demanding nature of the game) that the verbal aspect of this task overshadows the effects of referential robot gaze. These findings offer valuable insights for designing and validating robot gaze and turn-taking behavior in collaborative tasks which require coordination and efficient communication.

title: ANALYTICAL REVIEW OF TECHNOLOGICAL SUPPORT FOR THE REVERSE ENGINEERING OF CRITICAL GAS TURBINE COMPONENTS
