title: Comparative Evaluation of Gemini and DeepSeek for LLM-Generated Code Quality and Architectural Robustness in Backend Software Engineering
abstract: The increasing integration of large language models (LLMs) into software engineering workflows under the term vibe-coding necessitates systematic empirical evaluation of their code generation capabilities, especially in the context of complex backend development and architectural decision-making. This study compares popular foundational models Google Gemini 3 Pro and DeepSeek-V3.1 for developing a Java/Spring Boot backend application using a structured prompt-chaining protocol following a typical vibe-coding process. The generated solutions were evaluated using several quantitative and qualitative criteria, including the number of corrective prompts, the extent of required manual code interventions, functional correctness, architectural robustness, maintainability-related design choices, latency, and test quality. The results show substantial differences between the two models. DeepSeek required twice as many corrective natural language prompts as Gemini, but both models required a similar number of manual interventions in the generated code, with 23 for DeepSeek and 20 for Gemini. The most pronounced difference was in architectural reasoning. Gemini autonomously introduced the Data Transfer Object design pattern, resulting in a decoupled architecture, although at a cost of a minor performance issue. In contrast, DeepSeek was better in development of boilerplate code but exposed raw JPA entities through the application interface leading to tight coupling and other issues. Gemini’s solution satisfied 90.25% of evaluated requirements compared to 68.08% for DeepSeek. Additionally, generated tests showed a higher success rate and broader code coverage, achieving 95.7% successful test execution and 55.9% code coverage for Gemini, compared to 74.1% and 45.6% for DeepSeek, respectively. The results indicate that within the paradigm of vibe-coding, even the best available foundational LLMs may still require expert human supervision, especially when the generated code is expected to satisfy specific requirements in production-oriented backend systems.

title: Comparing human, LLM, and LLM-QFD approaches to technical requirement extraction
abstract: ABSTRACT: This study investigates how large language models (LLMs) support extracting technical requirements from early product pitches. Mechanical engineering students worked under three conditions: manual, LLM-assisted, and LLM combined with a QFD interface. Both AI-assisted conditions improved requirement quality and lowered perceived difficulty. Thematic analysis showed cognitive effort shifted from generating requirements to evaluating and verifying AI outputs, while the LLM-only group reported the most positive attitudes.

title: Comparison of OWL and AutomationML for Efficient Engineering Knowledge Representation
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Abstract—Representation of engineering knowledge is crucialfor complex automation system engineering, including knowledgesharing across engineering tools, model-driven orchestration ofcyber-physical production systems, as well as emerging integrationapproaches based on AI agents. Web Ontology Language(OWL) and AutomationML (AML) can be both perceived aswell-proven data representations and formats for representingand exchanging configuration and engineering knowledge relatedto production system components and automation system tools.This paper compares both representations, which is motivated bythe need for standardized or semi-standardized representationof configuration and integration in industrial applications. Themain objective of this paper is to compare the following keyfeatures of both representations: expressivity, formality, toolingsupport, modeling flexibility, reasoning capabilities, and communitysupport. Even though this topic is not brand new, it gainsnew attention in the emerging era of Large Language Models(LLMs), requiring efficient representation of knowledge. Thepaper explains benefits of both representations, and proposesto combine both by mapping AML to OWL and working withOWL representation of standardized AutomationML concepts.

title: Compiled AI: Deterministic Code Generation for LLM-Based Workflow Automation
abstract: We study compiled AI, a paradigm in which large language models generate executable code artifacts during a compilation phase, after which workflows execute deterministically without further model invocation. This paradigm has antecedents in prior work on declarative pipeline optimization (DSPy) and hybrid neural-symbolic planning (LLM+P); our contribution is a systems-oriented study of its application to high-stakes enterprise workflows, with particular emphasis on healthcare settings where reliability and auditability are critical. By constraining generation to narrow business-logic functions embedded in validated templates, compiled AI trades runtime flexibility for predictability, auditability, cost efficiency, and reduced security exposure. We introduce (i) a system architecture for constrained LLM-based code generation, (ii) a four-stage generation-and-validation pipeline that converts probabilistic model output into production-ready code artifacts, and (iii) an evaluation framework measuring operational metrics including token amortization, determinism, reliability, security, and cost. We evaluate on two task types: function-calling (BFCL, n=400) and document intelligence (DocILE, n=5,680 invoices). On function-calling, compiled AI achieves 96% task completion with zero execution tokens, breaking even with runtime inference at approximately 17 transactions and reducing token consumption by 57x at 1,000 transactions. On document intelligence, our Code Factory variant matches Direct LLM on key field extraction (KILE: 80.0%) while achieving the highest line item recognition accuracy (LIR: 80.4%). Security evaluation across 135 test cases demonstrates 96.7% accuracy on prompt injection detection and 87.5% on static code safety analysis with zero false positives.

title: Composite Technologies
abstract: This chapter builds upon the foundational understanding of elemental digital technologies discussed in Chapters 6 and 7 by shifting focus to Composite Technologies—advanced capabilities that emerge from the convergence of core digital functions such as computation, Data Management, instrumentation, and communication. Technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), Blockchain, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) exemplify how these foundational capabilities are integrated to deliver higher order, synergistic solutions that enable intelligent automation, cross-functional coordination, and adaptive business processes. Among these, packaged enterprise applications hold a particularly important place. Though they predate the Digital Era, their strategic relevance has been re-defined with the advent of the Cloud Platforms, AI integration, and real-time analytics. No longer limited to back-office functions, modern enterprise applications now act as dynamic platforms that support predictive insights, personalised experiences, and data-driven decision-making. This chapter explores how enterprise applications have become central to digital transformation efforts and how they contribute differentiated value in the AI-driven business landscape. The chapter also presents a structured framework for analysing Composite Technologies through the lens of digital taxonomy, offering a scalable approach for understanding both current and emerging technologies. This perspective can be extended to evaluate next-generation innovations such as robotics, agentic AI, and cyber–physical systems, which increasingly draw upon combinations of elemental capabilities to create complex, autonomous, and adaptive systems. While AI is introduced in this chapter as a Composite Technology, a more in-depth exploration of its foundations, paradigms, and business implications is presented in Chapter 9 .

title: Compound Fault Diagnosis for Industrial Machinery: Data-Driven Methods, Challenges, and LLM-Enhanced Perspectives
abstract: Compound faults occur when several local faults exist at the same time in industrial machinery and affect condition-monitoring signals together. Their signatures become mixed through modulation, structural transmission, operating-condition variation, and sensor response, which makes feature separation and state recognition more difficult. This paper reviews data-driven compound fault diagnosis from a scenario-oriented perspective. It first summarizes the task formulation and three main difficulties: coupled fault signatures, combinatorial growth of fault states, and distribution shifts across operating conditions and machines. The review then groups representative methods into three areas: signal representation, multi-label and fault-semantic modeling, and generalization under changing domains and unseen fault combinations. The paper also examines the emerging role of large language models, focusing on retrieval-augmented knowledge integration, evidence-grounded reasoning, tool-using diagnostic agents, and deployment reliability. It then points to several directions for future work, including compositional generalization, cross-machine transfer, multimodal sensing, industrial foundation models, and autonomous maintenance. Overall, the review argues that practical compound fault diagnosis depends on combining signal-level intelligence with reusable fault semantics and verifiable knowledge-based reasoning.

title: Comprehending possible manifestations and design aspects of embodied intelligence in next-generation cyber-physical systems
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the conceptual, architectural, and methodological foundations of cyber-physical systems (CPSs) featuring sensorimotor control. While generative and agentic AI have extended digital reasoning capabilities, embodied artificial intelligence (EAI) introduces a qualitatively distinct paradigm in which cognition is partially instantiated in morphology, materials, dynamics, and environmental interaction. This article develops a comprehensive theoretical and design-oriented framework for understanding and operationalizing embodiment in next-generation cyber-physical systems (NG-CPSs). The paper proceeds in six stages. First, it reconstructs the ontological evolution of CPSs from control-centric architectures to ecosystemic cognitive-material systems. Second, it articulates a systematic distinction between digital artificial intelligence (DAI) and EAI, clarifying their epistemological and functional differences. Third, it analyzes morphological computation and hybrid control architectures as foundational mechanisms of embodiment. Fourth, it formulates a taxonomy of embodiment-relevant system requirements and introduces the degree of embodiment (DoE) as a formal design metric. Fifth, it integrates embodied and agentic AI into a unified architectural framework. Sixth, it examines methodological, economic, and ethical implications of EAI encapsulated in the NG-CPS designs. The conceptual arguments are illustrated through the case of a full-body stroke rehabilitation (FBSR) system, demonstrating how embodied cognition enables real-time biomechanical co-regulation, adaptive proprioceptive scaffolding, and safe human–machine interaction beyond purely digital control. This position paper makes three original contributions. First, it formulates a unified theoretical framework that interprets embodiment as a distributed cognitive phenomenon spanning morphology, materials, dynamics, environment, and digital intelligence within NG-CPSs. Second, it introduces the DoE for evaluating the extent to which cognition is physically instantiated in NG-CPSs. Third, it demonstrates how EAI enables functionalities that cannot be implemented effectively through purely DAI deployment. The article concludes that strong embodiment is not universally necessary. Rather, its implementation should be justified by structural, functional, safety, environmental, and economic constraints. The findings support a paradigm shift from controlling physics with computation toward ‘computing’ through physics in the design of NG-CPSs.

title: Comprehensive benchmark of large language models for construction engineering and management
Comprehensive review of swarm intelligence for space robotics
abstract: Swarm intelligence has emerged as a transformative paradigm for autonomous space robotics, enabling scalable, robust, and adaptive behaviors through decentralized coordination of multiple agents. Inspired by collective phenomena in nature, swarm intelligence provides solutions to the challenges of extreme space environments, where resilience, autonomy, and fault tolerance are crucial. This review explores recent advances in the modeling, control, and validation of swarm-based space robotic systems. Mathematical frameworks ranging from single- and double-integrator dynamics to orbital swarm dynamics are examined, alongside formation control strategies such as consensus-based, leader–follower, virtual structure, and behavior-based approaches. The review covers swarm controllability, scalability, and performance metrics, highlighting trade-offs between efficiency, robustness, and computational complexity. Emerging optimization paradigms, including bio-inspired algorithms, hybrid global-local strategies, and multi-objective optimization, are surveyed for their applicability to mission-critical tasks such as debris removal, and distributed satellite constellations. The review also investigates numerical simulation platforms and experimental testbeds associated with swarm intelligence, highlighting their role in bridging the gap between theory and deployment. Case studies of current and proposed space missions illustrate the transition of swarm intelligence from conceptual design to operational reality, while trends in reinforcement learning, blockchain integration, and large language model-guided swarms signal future research directions. By consolidating theoretical foundations, experimental progress, and mission applications, this paper outlines the opportunities and challenges of harnessing swarm intelligence for future space exploration and infrastructure.

title: CompSphere AI: An AI-Powered Compliance Intelligence Platform for Chartered Accountants
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: CompSphere AI: An AI-Powered Compliance Intelligence Platform for Chartered Accountants This research paper presents a structured literature review of artificial intelligence technologies for improving compliance, auditing, and financial document processing workflows performed by Chartered Accountants (CAs). The study reviews 27 research papers published between 2019 and 2026, covering document intelligence, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), layout-aware transformers, financial Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), contradiction detection, Explainable AI (XAI), Robotic Process Automation (RPA), and agentic AI. The paper identifies key limitations in existing approaches, including unreliable financial reasoning, multilingual performance gaps, insufficient explainability, and the lack of integrated workflows that maintain an auditable chain of evidence. To address these challenges, the study proposes a four-layer reference architecture consisting of an Ingestion Layer, Reasoning Layer, Verification Layer, and Orchestration and Governance Layer. The proposed architecture emphasizes traceability, human oversight, model governance, and evidence-based compliance verification. The research also highlights opportunities for applying AI to Indian regulatory workflows, including Goods and Services Tax (GST), Tax Deducted at Source (TDS), Income Tax Returns (ITR), and Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) filings. This work aims to provide a foundation for developing reliable, explainable, and auditable AI-assisted compliance intelligence systems for Chartered Accountants. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Chartered Accountants, Financial Compliance, Document Intelligence, Large Language Models, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Explainable AI, Agentic AI, Regulatory Compliance, Financial Auditing.

title: Computational Cinematography using AI-Enabled Cameras, Autonomous Drones and Intelligent Scene Composition
abstract: Abstract Computational cinematography increasingly combines camera sensing, machine perception, autonomous platforms and creative decision support into a unified production intelligence layer. This book develops a research framework for AI-enabled cameras, autonomous drones and intelligent scene composition using only the supplied reference corpus. The camera is treated as a cyber-physical sensing system whose optical state, motion and scene context can be estimated, predicted and controlled, while aerial platforms are modelled as embodied camera agents operating under navigation uncertainty and safety constraints. The manuscript connects statistical modelling and causal evaluation with multimodal foundation models, scene representation, composition ranking, predictive control, reinforcement learning, digital twins, edge intelligence and reproducible MLOps. Particular attention is given to uncertainty propagation, human creative authority, selective automation, simulation-based verification and traceable evidence across capture and post-production workflows. Applied chapters translate the methods into feature-film production, virtual production, autonomous aerial capture, music and advertising, immersive media and resource-constrained production ecosystems. Global applicability is considered across South Asia, Europe, Africa and the Americas through designs that accommodate differences in regulation, connectivity, production scale and professional practice. The resulting architecture supports rigorous research while preserving artistic judgment, physical safety and accountable deployment. Keywords computational cinematography, AI-enabled cameras, autonomous drones, intelligent scene composition, camera intelligence, computational imaging, multimodal perception, scene understanding, visual grammar, autonomous cinematography, drone navigation, trajectory planning, safe reinforcement learning, predictive camera control, foundation models, edge AI, neuromorphic intelligence, digital twins, MLOps, camera telemetry, uncertainty calibration, trustworthy AI, virtual production, creative human–AI collaboration

title: Computational Design of Terrestrial Robots with Anisotropic Friction
abstract: Anisotropic friction is a critical source of propulsion for efficient locomotion of many terrestrial animals. The interplay between animal morphology, control, and anisotropically frictional contact makes designing optimal anisotropic friction for terrestrial locomotion intriguing and challenging. We propose a computational pipeline for co-designing anisotropic friction and controllers of terrestrial robots with diverse morphologies. Our pipeline presents a co-design algorithm that alternates between optimizing direction of anisotropic friction and training a neural network controller to improve the locomotion performance of a given robot morphology. Based on the intuition that controller’s performance does not change significantly when the frictional force differs slightly, we introduce the concept of trust-region into robot co-design, allowing the controller network to continue training from the previous iteration. Our evaluation on various morphologies show that anisotropic friction is critical for terrestrial robot locomotion, and our pipeline is statistically better than current state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we reveal that large language models (LLM) constitute a strong baseline for this kind of co-design problems, worth receiving more attention. We demonstrate that co-designing anisotropic friction and control unlocks effective locomotion in various downstream tasks, including locomotion on uneven terrain, navigation in a maze, and object manipulation. To validate our pipeline in the real world, we design and 3D print a variety of scales and systematically measure their anisotropic friction coefficients. Then we construct a multi-link robot with anisotropic scales designed by our pipeline and compare its performance with isotropic scales. Our real-world experiments confirm that isotropic scales are insufficient to support terrestrial robots’ locomotion abilities, and computationally co-designing friction and control enables robots to perform tasks including turning, slithering, and other non-trivial locomotion tasks.

title: Computational Experiments
abstract: A methodological framework for bridging the gap between Artificial Intelligence and Social Sciences Complex cyber-physical-social systems demand rigorous analysis, design, regulation and validation methods that traditional approaches cannot provide. Computational Experiments: A Bridge between Artificial Intelligence and Social Sciences delivers a systematic methodology spanning modeling, simulation, and validation of intelligent systems. Written by leading researchers in complex systems and artificial intelligence, this work provides both theoretical foundations and practical frameworks for studying intricate social and physical systems. The book covers the artificial society modeling framework across four levels: AI agents and prospect theory, learning mechanisms of AI agents, AI society and social networks, and integration with environmental systems. It addresses how computational experiments incorporate generative agents and large language models, and explores policy sandboxes for decision analysis and social system behavior prediction in complex contexts. The book also discusses: Comprehensive coverage of computational experiment methodology including origins, development history, and knowledge frameworks essential for practical applications Social simulation technology foundations providing unique insights into simulating and deducing complex social systems from interdisciplinary research perspectives Detailed exploration of AI agent architectures incorporating prospect theory, ??reinforcement learning mechanisms, and multi-agent coordination strategies for ??system modeling Frameworks for integrating virtual and real-world intelligence to improve predictive capabilities and support decision-making in complex operational environments Designed for professors, researchers, and graduate students in computer science, artificial intelligence, social computing, and systems engineering, this book also serves professionals in policy simulation, strategic planning, and smart system development who require rigorous methods for validating intelligent system behavior.

title: Computational Ontology & Creation (COC): A Formal Framework for the Construction, Evolution, and Verification of Digital Realities
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Abstract Current paradigms in Artificial Intelligence focus predominantly on probabilistic generation from data distributions, often resulting in high-entropy outputs lacking causal consistency (known as "hallucinations"). This paper proposes a paradigm shift from learning patterns to constructing realities, formally establishing a new high-dimensional discipline: Computational Ontology & Creation (COC). Building upon the engineering protocols of WorldSeed (Zhang, 2025), this work investigates the mathematical structure, evolutionary dynamics, and logical boundaries of possible digital worlds. It aims to construct low-entropy, logically self-consistent entities out of the maximum-entropy void through formal axiomatic constraints. Key Contributions: The SABO Algebra: Introduces the formal tuple ⟨S, A, B, O⟩ (State, Action, Boundary, Observer) as the fundamental formalism for defining digital entities and their evolutionary dynamics. Canonical Slices of Reality: Demonstrates the universality of the framework by mathematically deriving the canonical slices of Physics, Computation, Biology, and Economics as specific parameter configurations of the meta-interface. The Trinity of Limits: Delineates the three absolute horizons that bound the discipline: the Shannon Limit (Lower Bound), Gödel's Incompleteness (Upper Bound), and Computational Irreducibility (Outer Bound). Axiomatic Decoding: Proposes a novel inference-time intervention mechanism to mitigate LLM hallucinations by introducing explicit "Boundary" constraints into the decoding process. Meta-Ethics: Establishes a foundational ethical framework for the "Meta-Era," including the Creator's Liability and the Alignment Convergence. This document serves as the founding manifesto for the WorldSeed Institute and the discipline of COC, marking the transition of AI development from "Alchemy" to "Architecture."

title: Computer-aided innovation for intelligent product design: a text mining and knowledge management approach
abstract: The fast-paced innovation and the growing need for user-centric products hold traditional design approaches against the wall in the Industry 4.0 era. This research establishes a unified Computer-Aided Innovation (CAI) framework based on text mining, ontology-based knowledge management, and TRIZ-based reasoning to support intelligent product design. The framework uses natural language processing to extract user requirements, technical problems, and potential contradictions from unstructured textual content sources such as product reviews, patents, and technical information. These insights are then structured in a TRIZ-compliant knowledge base to enable the rapid, transparent, and traceable generation of concepts. A smart wearable health device was used as the case study to evaluate the system's performance, and the results showed that the ideation efficiency of all concepts was significantly improved, with all concepts produced in less than 20 minutes, and the results were balanced across novelty, feasibility, and usability metrics. Compared with traditional methods such as brainstorming and Quality Function Deployment (QFD), the proposed framework yielded richer insights, greater concept diversity, and more evidence-based recommendations. Despite these advantages, the approach appears sensitive to textual ambiguity, domain-specific terminology, and the long-term scalability of the ontology repository. Future research will focus on the following areas: leveraging multilingual data sources, combining generative AI with digital twin simulations for time-critical design exploration, and expanding the framework to other product domains. Overall, the proposed CAI framework is part of promoting systematic innovation by incorporating AI-assisted reasoning and structured knowledge representation in the early stages of product design.

title: Computer-aided Management and Compliance Review of Engineering Specifications Based on Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model
Conceptual Engineering Using Large Language Models
Conceptualising Health Economic Models Using a Graph Retrieval-Augmented, Agentic AI Framework with Human-in-the-Loop Validation: Proof-of-Concept Study
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Health economic models (HEMs) are crucial for assessing the cost-effectiveness of healthcare interventions, informing policy decisions and guiding reimbursement strategies. This study examines the feasibility of employing generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) for the conceptualisation of HEMs. Two proof-of-concept studies were conducted, implementing a first-of-its-kind agentic Gen-AI-augmented approach for model conceptualisation. METHODS: An agentic Gen-AI framework was developed, incorporating the chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning algorithm through advanced prompt engineering, compounded with self-consistency, executed in an external Python programming environment. Within this framework, an agentic execution layer (the 'agent') autonomously orchestrated a multi-step retrieval-reasoning-generation task. Additionally, a graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technique was implemented by linking the large language model (LLM) to an external database curated with user-selected data specific to HEM. Two case studies were explored: breast cancer, representing a data-rich disease area, and transthyretin amyloid polyneuropathy (ATTR-PN), exemplifying a data-sparse rare disease. RESULTS: The agentic Gen-AI framework successfully generated two key outputs that were subsequently validated against published literature and expert review from health economic (HE) modelers and clinicians: (1) a disease concept diagram illustrating the progression of the disease and its associated health states, and (2) a model structure diagram depicting patient transitions between various health states. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that Gen-AI-augmented methodologies can enhance multiple aspects of HEM conceptualisation, including problem definition, disease and treatment effect pathway development, model structure recommendations, and drafting of model specification plans. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first study to integrate cutting-edge Gen-AI techniques such as human-in-the-loop (HITL), chain of thought-self-consistency (CoT-SC), and graph-based RAG for HEM conceptualisation or broader health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) applications.

title: Conceptualizing a framework for GenAI approaches in Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF): A review
abstract: This review explores the integration touch points for emerging Generative AI (GenAI) tools in various aspects of the Additive Manufacturing (AM) process chain, emphasizing application-specific design and optimization strategies. Over the past two decades, AM has evolved into a transformative manufacturing paradigm, enabling the realization of complex geometries and multi-material constructs with tailored functional properties. AM techniques such as Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF) have particularly matured to a point of democratizing AM methods for end users. Concurrently, the emergence of advanced sensing technologies and automation has enabled the adoption of AI-driven methodologies across the AM workflow. Despite these advancements, the underlying algorithmic frameworks, training protocols, and tunability for different target application functionalities exhibit substantial heterogeneity. This paper aims to consolidate the literature reports into a concurrent framework toward a function-driven design approach. Specifically, the authors identify various touch points for AI/ML approaches in design, manufacturing, and part performance within various stages of the AM workflow. Furthermore, potential opportunities for emerging GenAI approaches within the proposed concurrent framework are also presented.

title: Conceptualizing Cognitive and Agentic Digital Twins
venue: International Multidisciplinary Journal of Emerging Technologies and Applications
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) have extended beyond the original concept of a static digital model, to a dynamic, data-driven, and increasingly intelligent cyber-physical structure, which underlies modern Industry 4.0 systems. The paper gives a comprehensive and integrative conceptualization of DTs, Cognitive Digital Twins (CDTs), and agentic AI-enhanced DTs through an organized narrative literature review which synthesizes the foundational definitions, the theoretical differences between DTs and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), and the evolution of Digital Models and Digital Shadows to fully synchronous, two-way DTs. The research synthesizes the major architectural models, such as layered, multi-dimensional, cognitive and agentic models, and discusses the facilitating technologies that enable real-time synchronization, semantic reasoning, and autonomous decision-making. The state-of-the-art analysis indicates that the key research trends include ecosystem-based DTs, AI-driven analytics, semantic enrichment, and the development of LLM-enabled agentic DTs that are able to plan and coordinate actions in a goal-oriented manner. The paper also compares industrial and open-source DT platforms, outlines the present-day limitations in semantic interoperability, cognitive integration, and autonomy and demonstrates real-world applications in manufacturing, healthcare, smart cities, and energy systems. The discussion proposes future research directions such as standardized cognitive layers, safe LLM grounding, multi-DT coordination, and governance frameworks of autonomous DT ecosystems. Overall, the paper contributes a unified conceptual model and a holistic synthesis that connects theory, architecture, technology, and application, providing a foundation for advancing the next generation of intelligent Digital Twin systems.

title: ConDA: A constraint discovery agent for cross-system optimization of manufacturing operations
Connecting AAS and LLMs for Controlling NDT Devices
abstract: The ongoing development and implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) is opening up new ways to increase efficiency and improve quality of processes, including the process of non-destructive testing (NDT). Traditional AI applications, which focus on analyzing existing processes, are recently being supplemented by generative AI models that dynamically generate content such as text, images, or videos and thereby facilitate intuitive human-machine interactions. The following report describes how generative AI is used in non-destructive testing (NDT) to optimize testing processes through more efficient data processing, precise information provision, and bidirectional AI-machine interaction. This includes the development of an assistance system that processes NDT-relevant expert knowledge and integrates device information to optimize inspection processes and support experts. The use of technologies such as the "asset administration shell" (AAS) and "OPC UA" (Open Platform Communication Unified Architecture) enables real-time data manipulation and admits bidirectional interaction with the testing devices. The dynamic adaptation of the system to user needs allows testing devices to actively intervene in the testing process, or, with regard to digital certificates, to check the suitability of the device or create digital test reports.

title: Consilience for Verifier-Free Test-Time Scaling
abstract: Test-time scaling often uses an external verifier, such as compilers and test cases in coding or trained value functions in robotics applications, to obtain high-quality rollouts. Verifier-free test-time scaling (or VF-TTS) is gaining extensive attention as a mechanism to enhance Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning, primarily because we do not have access to such high-quality verifiers in many real-world applications. Among existing VF-TTS methods, confidence-based VF-TTS methods, which compute and rank rollouts solely by confidence, are particularly promising. Such methods introduce near-zero overhead for sample evaluation and require minimal access to internal model states, making the methods highly flexible across models and tasks. In this paper, we demonstrate a critical limitation of existing confidence-based VF-TTS methods by showing that such methods catastrophically break down on complex tasks. We observe a very interesting phenomenon: uniformly high confidence frequently indicates a failure to explore, favoring confidently wrong answers. To address this, our core insight is that robust cognitive search requires a specific confidence trajectory pattern: such methods perform exploratory branching at the beginning, as manifested by low initial confidence, and converge to a high final confidence solution. To implement this insight, we introduce consilience, a novel selection framework that explicitly evaluates the temporal asymmetry of confidence in reasoning. We operationalize this via a combinatorial metric that actively penalizes high initial confidence while strictly demanding final certainty. Extensive experiments covering both graduate-level mathematics problems and free-form code generation demonstrate that consilience effectively outperforms existing baselines, validating our novel perspective on completion confidence.

title: Consistency-Preserving Hybrid Ontology Reconstruction for Heterogeneous Manufacturing Ontologies
abstract: Ontology reconstruction across multiple heterogeneous manufacturing sources remains a persistent challenge in smart manufacturing, where independently developed information systems often yield semantically fragmented and structurally incompatible knowledge representations. Existing ontology alignment and merging approaches mainly focus on local correspondence identification and post-hoc repair, which limits their ability to preserve global structural coherence and logical consistency during large-scale ontology integration. This paper proposes a consistency-preserving hybrid ontology reconstruction method (HMOR) for multi-source heterogeneous data. HMOR reconstructs a unified ontology through a core ontology-guided process that integrates hybrid semantic mapping, structural normalization, and incremental consistency verification within a single framework. A core manufacturing ontology (CMO) is introduced as a semantic pivot to mediate heterogeneous source ontologies and regularize the reconstruction space. In addition, a constraint-aware repair mechanism is embedded into the reconstruction process to detect and resolve semantic conflicts at an early stage, thereby reducing inconsistency propagation. From a theoretical perspective, the proposed framework preserves logical consistency throughout reconstruction. Furthermore, to validate its practical applicability in computer-integrated manufacturing, HMOR was deployed in a real-world industrial case study involving a centrifugal compressor rotor flexible assembly line. By deploying the framework within a cloud-edge-end architecture, the semantic integration of physical robotic workstations, PLCs, and digital twin services was successfully achieved. Experimental and industrial results show that HMOR consistently outperforms representative baseline methods in consistency preservation, reconstruction completeness, and semantic retention. The findings further demonstrate strong robustness under increasing conflict intensity, favorable scalability, and the capability to manage large-scale concurrent industrial connections in real-time, suggesting that HMOR provides a robust semantic infrastructure for complex smart manufacturing scenarios.

title: Constellation: Lossless Document Structuring via Control-Data Flow Decoupling
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Accurately transforming unstructured documents into structured intermediate representations (such as Markdown or JSON) with hierarchical semantics is the core foundation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), automated knowledge graph construction, and large language model (LLM) context engineering. However, traditional pure-rule-based parsing engines suffer from severe hierarchy loss when handling non-standard formatting. On the other hand, end-to-end LLM extraction paradigms face two insurmountable inherent flaws: first, uncontrollable generative hallucinations caused by autoregressive mechanisms lead to text alteration, making them unusable in strict domains requiring absolute fidelity; second, the output token cost for full-text rewriting is prohibitively high. To address these issues, we propose the \textbf{Constellation} document parsing architecture, which achieves strict decoupling of the semantic control flow and data transfer flow at the system level. The LLM acts solely as a "control center" to output low-dimensional spatial anchors and hierarchical judgments (control flow), while the underlying deterministic finite state machine (FSM) directly extracts and losslessly assembles the original characters based on these anchors (data flow). The parsed result is a native JSON document tree that can be zero-cost serialized into any downstream format. Over benchmark datasets ranging from 1.9M to 10.07M characters, the architecture not only achieves zero character-level loss at the physical extraction layer but also effectively resolves hierarchical misalignment in long texts. In horizontal comparisons with IBM Docling and Microsoft MarkItDown, Constellation achieved a hierarchy accuracy of 1.0000 in extreme non-standard scenarios lacking explicit heading styles, whereas rule-based schemes degraded to 0.0000. This research provides a new paradigm with low computational overhead and absolute fidelity for precise document parsing in the LLM era.

title: Constrained Hybrid AI for Smart Classroom Audiovisual Diagnosis
abstract: Smart classrooms are consumer-scale cyber-physical systems in which heterogeneous audiovisual (AV) failures must be diagnosed and resolved within a strict pre-class window. Conventional rule-based self-checking is fast but brittle under closed-world assumptions, while purely data-driven AI is difficult to deploy safely due to limited training data and the risk of unsafe actions on physical devices. This article presents a constrained hybrid diagnostic architecture, studied as an early deployment and integration effort, that combines deterministic rule-based self-checking, non-intrusive physical verification, and a large language model (LLM) used only as a constrained diagnostic planner. The system separates diagnostic reasoning from physical execution: rules and LLM proposals are represented as auditable check actions, all actions are routed through a policy enforcement point, and unsafe or high-impact requests are rejected before reaching devices. Controlled fault-injection experiments on a representative smart classroom testbed covered ten predefined fault categories and 100 repeated runs, while the architecture was deployed in 70 real classrooms. In this controlled setting, the constrained LLM planner achieved 99% accuracy of root-cause identification, generated safe diagnostic paths when rule priors were incomplete, reduced a representative symptom-driven diagnosis from 38 static checks to 7 checks, and produced 14 unsafe or out-of-scope requests, all of which were successfully blocked by the policy layer.

title: Constraining LLM-Based RDF Generation with Ontology-Guided Prompting in Urban Agriculture
venue: Anais do XLI Simpósio Brasileiro de Banco de Dados (SBBD 2026)
abstract: The construction and maintenance of knowledge graphs remain labor-intensive tasks, particularly when relevant information is available primarily in semi-structured textual sources. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for automating knowledge graph population, yet generating RDF instances that comply with ontology constraints remains challenging. This paper investigates an ontology-guided prompting strategy for generating RDF knowledge graphs from textual descriptions of horticultural cultivars. The proposed approach embeds a domain ontology together with modeling patterns derived from established semantic standards and provides explicit schema definitions, anchored instances, and few-shot RDF/Turtle examples within the prompt. The method is evaluated on a dataset of 42 cultivar webpages using SHACL-based validation, precision–recall analysis, and hallucination detection. Results show that ontology-guided prompting substantially improves structural validity and semantic accuracy while significantly reducing hallucinated assertions.

title: Constraint-Aware Graph Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Multimodal Industrial Surface Defect Diagnosis
Constraint-Aware LLM Pipeline for EvoGym Environment Generation with Fitness-Guided Prompt Refinement
venue: International Conference on Innovative Trends in Information Technology (ICITIIT)
abstract: Soft robotics focuses on flexible, deformable robots that can be designed through simulation. In this article, A LLaMEA-inspired, fitness-guided prompt mutation framework for EvoGym, demonstrating simulator-constrained LLM environment generation validated via agent traversal behavior as feasibility evidence has been shown. Existing papers like mutates and selects algorithms based on performance metrics and feedback from runtime, can be extended to find if it supports enhancing generation of environments which support agent's explorative ability. LLM-driven evolutionary prompting used to generate environments appropriate to evogym. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the suggested approach produces environments with higher physical relevance, superior structural diversity, and improved compatibility compared to those designed using baseline LLM prompting methods.

title: Constraint-Guided In-Context Learning for Domain-Specific Triplet Extraction
abstract: The automation of high-quality knowledge graph construction hinges on the precise extraction of relational triplets from unstructured text. While large language models (LLMs) offer potential solutions, current approaches remain limited in specialized domains due to their reliance on manual annotation and model fine-tuning. Crucially, the absence of explicit constraints on knowledge reasoning introduces significant uncertainty and errors in domain-specific triplet extraction. To address these gaps, this study proposes OntoP2KG, a novel framework integrating domain ontology constraints with structured prompt engineering. The method first identifies domain-subdomain attributes of input text, retrieves relevant concepts from ontologies and few-shot examples, and constructs a knowledge-enriched context. Subsequently, through structured prompts, the LLM is guided to perform accurate triplet extraction, followed by redundancy resolution based on graph embedding similarity and rule matching. Experimental results demonstrate that OntoP2KG significantly improves precision and recall in domain triplet extraction without requiring parameter fine-tuning, providing a robust path toward automated construction of domain-specific knowledge graphs.

title: Constructing Certified Convergence: The Principle of Naturality, Part I
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The Principle of Naturality (PN) is an explainable neuro-symbolic framework for detecting latent convergences among actors whose root premises are mutually exclusive. Its defining feature — and what sets it apart — is explainability: what the framework emits is not an opaque agreement score but a structured, auditable explanation of each convergence: the meeting point (a HUB), the per-actor inferential paths that reach it, the per-pair certificates that license it, and the normative justification for why that point was selected. The mechanism. Each actor's stance is expanded into an actor-relative inferential tree (P -> Q -> R -> ...), in which edges are defeasible inferential commitments — not formally valid deductions or strict causation — and each root-to-leaf branch reads as one possible line of reasoning. Cross-actor proposition pairs are validated by a three-stage cascade: an embedding pre-filter (S-BERT), bidirectional NLI with DeBERTa under pragmatic normalization with a contradiction veto, and an LLM role-inversion verification. Validated fusions are grouped with the Union-Find algorithm into connected components; within each, strict HUBs are closed multipartite cliques (pairwise certified across all actors) and lax HUBs are sets with complete cross-actor coverage. The selected HUB minimizes, lexicographically, the Total Topological Friction (TTF), a bicomposite path cost that balances displacement from each actor's root position against relevance to the dispute. The normative half. The selection rule is characterized as a Pareto-efficient utilitarian bargaining solution (4/4 cases), distinct from the Nash solution — which in GERD prefers a more balanced split — and from the egalitarian one. This makes the model's distributive commitment explicit and debatable, which is part of the explanation rather than a verdict. Evaluation. Four heterogeneous cases: the fictional control Selene (isolating the result from memorization), GERD (geopolitical, three states), Lia Lee (intercultural bioethics), and an intrapersonal conflict modeled from Bipolar I narratives (two antagonistic cognitive states within a single individual, with no architectural change). Against geometric baselines (cosine thresholding, single-linkage, k-means) none exceeds 7% precision; a stage ablation shows that the symbolic stages are what supply precision; and the convergences are shown not to be an artifact of depth-driven semantic collapse. Topological Data Analysis (Mapper, Vietoris-Rips persistence) is a post-hoc layer that visualizes the shape of the disagreement, with permutation tests confirming structured cross-actor separation (the strongest pair reaching z > 9). A descriptive mediation probe. An external proposal is tested against each actor's frozen tree — the trees are not re-expanded toward the proposal, since that would manufacture convergence by construction — which guarantees that a detected support is genuine. title: Constructing Industrial-Scale Optimization Modeling Benchmark
abstract: Optimization modeling underpins decision-making in logistics, manufacturing, energy, and finance, yet translating natural-language requirements into correct optimization formulations and solver-executable code remains labor-intensive. Although large language models (LLMs) have been explored for this task, evaluation is still dominated by toy-sized or synthetic benchmarks, masking the difficulty of industrial problems with $10^{3}$--$10^{6}$ (or more) variables and constraints. A key bottleneck is the lack of benchmarks that align natural-language specifications with reference formulations/solver code grounded in real optimization models. To fill in this gap, we introduce MIPLIB-NL, built via a structure-aware reverse construction methodology from real mixed-integer linear programs in MIPLIB~2017. Our pipeline (i) recovers compact, reusable model structure from flat solver formulations, (ii) reverse-generates natural-language specifications explicitly tied to this recovered structure under a unified model--data separation format, and (iii) performs iterative semantic validation through expert review and human--LLM interaction with independent reconstruction checks. This yields 223 one-to-one reconstructions that preserve the mathematical content of the original instances while enabling realistic natural-language-to-optimization evaluation. Experiments show substantial performance degradation on MIPLIB-NL for systems that perform strongly on existing benchmarks, exposing failure modes invisible at toy scale.

title: Construction method of knowledge enhanced industrial-LLM for intelligent manufacturing operation and maintenance
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 5th International Conference on Cyber Security, Artificial Intelligence and Digital Economy
abstract: In response to the limitations of general retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods in handling term ambiguity and multi-hop causal reasoning in industrial scenarios, this paper proposes a knowledge-enhanced industrial large language model construction method for intelligent manufacturing operation and maintenance. It integrates knowledge graph entity alignment with RAG to enable dynamic knowledge recall, and employs low-rank adaptation for efficient fine-tuning using multi-source heterogeneous operation and maintenance data. The method also incorporates a constraint decoding mechanism based on real-time knowledge graph verification to suppress hallucinations and ensure output interpretability. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in fault diagnosis accuracy and maintenance plan generation quality compared to baseline models.

title: Construction of a Knowledge Graph for Functional Specification Standards of Traditional Chinese Medicine Information Systems Based on Large Language Models
abstract: Objective: To address the issue of fragmented knowledge in functional specification documents for Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) information systems and enable the querying and improve the readability of standard knowledge. Methods: Using 22 functional specification standard documents related to TCM information systems from the group standards issued by the China Association of Chinese Medicine Informatics as the data source, we designed domain-constrained prompts based on the CRISPE framework to guide the DeepSeek large language model in extracting entities and relations. We then integrated rule-based constraints to construct the knowledge graph. Results: A knowledge graph consisting of 2294 nodes and 6330 relations was generated. The graph structure is clear and semantically consistent, capable of efficiently supporting queries and visualization. Conclusion: The construction method based on large language models and prompt engineering proposed in this study is effective, providing a new approach for knowledge graph construction in related fields. Future work can integrate multi-domain data to further enhance the value of the graph.

title: Construction of Bridge Maintenance Knowledge Graph Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Bridge maintenance decision-making is challenged by the “data-rich but knowledge-poor” nature of unstructured inspection and maintenance reports. A bridge maintenance knowledge graph (BMKG) construction framework is proposed, developed from a corpus of 275 inspection reports, to enable structured representation of engineering knowledge and decision support. A standards-aligned domain ontology provides semantic constraints for downstream information extraction and organization. Building on this ontology, a RoBERTa–BiGRU–CRF named entity recognition (NER) model is developed, achieving a precision of 90.8%, recall of 93.8%, and a micro-averaged F1-score (micro-F1) of 92.3%. Inter-annotator agreement for the NER annotations was quantified using Cohen’s kappa, yielding κ = 0.86. To avoid the cost of large-scale relation annotation, relations are constructed using interpretable, rule-based constraints. Through manual verification audit of randomly sampled relationship instances under a strict exact-match criterion (i.e., requiring exact matches for entity boundaries, entity types, and relationship types), an overall manual verification rate of 93.67% was obtained. Unlike existing KG methods that rely heavily on annotated data, the BMKG framework integrates ontological constraints with a rule-driven approach, prioritizing interpretability and reducing dependency on large-scale relation labeling. Consequently, the resulting knowledge graph supports semantic retrieval and visual exploration, enabling efficient disease-to-recommendation queries for refined bridge maintenance management.
