title: Industrial agents: Architecture, key technologies, and future perspectives
abstract: The advancement of new-generation artificial intelligence technologies, such as industrial foundation models and embodied AI, has catalyzed the emergence of new agents oriented towards Agentic AI, presenting fresh opportunities for the development of industrial artificial intelligence. As novel agent systems driven by these cutting-edge technologies and serving the full lifecycle of industrial products, industrial agents encompass both embodied and non-embodied (software system) forms. They possess core capabilities tailored to industrial scenarios, including perception and understanding, knowledge memory, planning and decision-making, communication and interaction, autonomous execution, and evolutionary learning. Consequently, they provide intelligent services across the entire business chain of industrial manufacturing, including R&D, manufacturing, testing, management, and maintenance. Currently, systematic research regarding new-generation industrial agents remains a gap in the field. This paper defines the concept of industrial agents and analyzes their key characteristics. It proposes an architecture for industrial agents comprising three layers: the industrial agent base, the industrial agent system, and industrial applications, while also elucidating the associated key technologies. Centering on industrial product lifecycle activities, the paper discusses typical future application scenarios for agents in R&D, manufacturing, testing, management, and maintenance. Finally, the paper provides an outlook on the future development of industrial agents, analyzing prospective technical directions such as the industrial agent foundation, industrial world models, software-hardware synergetic agents, trustworthy agents with long-term memory, endogenous security, and standardization. This work provides a systematic reference for the construction of theoretical and technical frameworks, system development, and industrial application of industrial agents driven by new-generation AI.

title: Industrial and Manufacturing Generative AI: Bibliographic, Keyword, and Thematic Dataset (2022–2026)
abstract: This dataset contains the data used for a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of applications of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) in industrial and manufacturing contexts. The dataset includes 373 peer-reviewed academic sources published between 2022 and 2026 and retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, and ACM Digital Library. The selected publications focus on GAI-related methods and applications, including generative design, large language models, diffusion models, generative adversarial networks, foundation models, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, electronic design automation, additive manufacturing, materials discovery, smart manufacturing, robotics, digital twins, and human–AI collaboration. The dataset provides the final deduplicated bibliographic corpus, normalized author-keyword tables, keyword-normalization thesaurus, thematic coding sheet, binary document–keyword matrix, and co-occurrence-analysis outputs. It supports reproducibility of the bibliometric analysis, keyword normalization, thematic classification, and co-occurrence analysis presented in the review. Main validation values: 373 final records; 340 records with available author keywords; 1,806 normalized keyword instances; 1,070 globally unique normalized keywords; 530 top-20 keyword-frequency occurrences; 528 binary top-20 document–keyword assignments; and 107 non-zero co-occurrence edges.

title: Industrial Applications of AI in Aircraft Manufacturing: A PRISMA Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Aircraft industry, especially the commercial aircraft branch, is an important and specific field in manufacturing due to its distinct features such as high personalization and low production output, and is expected to grow significantly in the future. At the same time, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have undertaken a major revolution in the manufacturing sector with promising improvements. However, the global deployment of AI/ML in the aircraft manufacturing sphere still requires further operationalization. This study aims to address the challenges of this implementation by providing a PRISMA systematic literature review of 89 articles. Several perspectives were analyzed, including word cloud analysis, distribution over the years, geographical distribution, domains of application, learning paradigms, machine learning models, materials, and components. Additionally, a synthesis was conducted on data augmentation, data reduction, hardware employed, and an overall synthesis of all relevant articles in this field. The findings revealed insights into the major trends of AI/ML applications in terms of techniques, global influence, applications, materials and components. This study contributes to the field by gathering the present state-of-the-art research, identifying its key elements, and highlighting further research opportunities, such as the use of LLMs and the integration of human factors.

title: Industrial Artificial Intelligence: A Review of Technologies, Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI) has emerged as a transformative paradigm that integrates advanced computational intelligence with industrial systems, enabling unprecedented levels of automation, optimization, and decision support across manufacturing and process industries. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of IAI technologies, spanning machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, digital twins, and explainable AI, and examines their deployment across diverse industrial sectors including automotive, aerospace, energy, logistics, and semiconductor manufacturing. Key application domains, including predictive maintenance, quality control, process optimization, and supply chain management, are critically analyzed in terms of methodology, performance benchmarks, and deployment maturity. Unlike prior reviews that focus primarily on a single technology family or a single application domain, this review integrates technology, application, and challenge perspectives within one evidence-based framework and benchmarks technology maturity against deployment readiness across eight industrial sectors. The review further identifies persistent challenges such as data scarcity, black-box opacity, legacy system integration, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and workforce readiness, and proposes evidence-based mitigation strategies for each. A forward-looking perspective is offered, highlighting the convergence of large language models, federated learning, and Industry 5.0 human-centric frameworks as defining trajectories for the next decade. Drawing on 40 peer-reviewed journal articles identified through a systematic literature search, this article serves as a structured foundation for researchers, engineers, and policymakers navigating the complex IAI landscape.

title: Industrial Financial Risk Prediction Model Based on Graph Neural Network and Knowledge Graph Inference
venue: Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers
abstract: With the increasing complexity of the global financial market and the surge in data volume, how to effectively predict and avoid industrial financial risks has become a key issue that financial institutions and regulators need to address. Traditional prediction methods are often limited by the limitations of data representation and the ability of models to deal with complex relationships, while graph neural networks (GNNs) and knowledge graphs (KGs) provide a new perspective and means to solve these problems. This study constructs a KG covering a wide range of industrial financial information, which not only contains the direct correlation between industries but also incorporates rich background knowledge and semantic information. A novel GNN architecture is designed, which can make full use of the structured information in the KG to learn the potential correlations and dependencies between industries. Experimental results show that compared with the existing industrial financial risk prediction models, the proposed model has significant advantages in forecasting accuracy, stability and generalization ability. Especially when dealing with complex and changeable industrial financial data, the model can more accurately capture potential risk factors and provide timely and reliable risk early warning for financial institutions. The industrial financial risk prediction model based on GNN and KG reasoning proposed in this study provides a new and effective solution for industrial financial risk prediction. The model not only improves the accuracy and robustness of the forecast but also provides financial institutions with more intelligent and refined risk management tools.

title: Industrial-grade trustworthy embodied system for power battery disassembly based on the disassembly NeuroSymbolic World Model
Industrial-Instruction: A source-grounded question answering dataset from industrial technical reports for training and evaluating large language models
abstract: Industrial technical reports contain high-value knowledge for maintenance, troubleshooting and product engineering, but their heterogeneous structure, including dense prose, specifications and tables, makes them difficult to index and reason over with standard retrieval and question-answering pipelines. This article describes Industrial-Instruction, a retrieval-grounded question-answering dataset derived from 906 publicly available Panasonic technical documents comprising 7,525 pages. The source PDFs were collected manually from the Panasonic website and converted to Markdown with the Dots.OCR vision-language model, preserving both running text and tabular content. Images were discarded so that the released data is purely textual. After removal of empty, near-empty and duplicate pages, the remaining pages were embedded with EmbeddingGemma and indexed with FAISS to form a semantic knowledge base. Multiple-choice question-answer instances were then synthesized against retrieved evidence from this knowledge base under five explicitly modeled query-document relationships: irrelevant retrieval (r0), single-document support (r1), multi-document support (r2), single-document answer (r3) and multi-document answer (r4). Two parallel versions of the dataset were produced using the identical pipeline, prompts and scenario definitions, differing only in the generator model: one using the open-weight Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct model and one using the closed, API-based Claude-Opus-4.6 model. Rule-based filters were applied to both runs to enforce the multiple-choice option structure and answer format, reducing 23,910 raw pairs to 13,557 for the open-weight version and 26,395 raw pairs to 26,252 for the frontier-model version. Each version is distributed with a held-out benchmark split of 1,000 items, balanced across the five scenarios. Each record stores the question, answer key, five answer options and the source documents retrieved when the item was generated. The data are released in the standard Hugging Face format. They can be reused to instruction-tune and benchmark retrieval-augmented language models on real industrial documentation, study robustness to retrieval noise and multi-step evidence integration, and compare open-weight and frontier models as synthetic data generators under otherwise identical conditions.

title: Industrial Internet of Agents: Conceptual Architecture, Applications, and Challenges
abstract: AI agents driven by foundation models have shown potential for industrial automation beyond rule-based control. However, existing studies mainly examine single agents or multi-agent systems with fixed roles, leaving networked coordination among heterogeneous industrial agents insufficiently explored. This paper examines the intersection of networked agents and industrial automation, where industrial signals, communication constraints, contextual information, and operational requirements must be considered jointly. It introduces the Industrial Internet of Agents (IIoA) and presents a conceptual architecture for analyzing industrial deployment requirements. Building on the Internet of Agents (IoA) framework, IIoA re-specifies sensing, communication, decision-making, and execution through eleven industrial extensions, including industrial signal awareness, operational technology (OT) protocol bridging, tiered latency design, feasibility-coupled planning, and semantic execution gateways. Representative studies are synthesized across shopfloor operations, autonomous plant operation and maintenance, supply chain collaboration, and digital twin systems. The analysis indicates that industrial agent networking requires the joint design of semantic coordination, OT interoperability, latency-aware deployment, trust governance, and verifiable physical execution. Finally, seven open challenges are identified, covering reliability, latency, protocol integrity, scalability, physical grounding, adaptability, and evaluation.

title: Industrial knowledge-enhanced fault diagnosis method: Integrating LLM and knowledge graph for fault reasoning and maintenance recommendation in CNC machine tools
INDUSTRIAL KNOWLEDGE GRAPHS FOR OPERATIONAL TECHNOLOGY DEFENCE: FROM NETWORK FLOWS TO TRACEABLE SECURITY ANALYSIS
abstract: Operational technology (OT) environments in industrial manufacturing rely on hundreds of networked devices whose security-relevant data such as network topology, asset identity, firmware, vulnerability, network traffic and regulatory requirements are distributed across multiple isolated systems with no standard integration mechanism.This fragmentation prevents security analysts from obtaining a complete, consistent, and auditable view of which assets are present, which are exposed to known vulnerabilities, and how a compromise could propagate through the network. This thesis investigates how heterogeneous OT data sources can be systematically integrated into a multi-layer knowledge graph to provide asset visibility that is (i) unified, with all data sources queryable in a single graph; (ii) measurable, through enrichment coverage metrics of each layer; and (iii) traceable, with every finding linked through explicit graph relationships to its underlying evidence. The thesis further investigates whether this representation enables effective blast-radius analysis by combining structural topology and behaviour-driven communication analysis into a unified and traceable security analysis framework. Three main contributions distinguish this work. First, a multi-layer architecture implemented in Neo4j, integrates topology, machine abstraction, asset identity, vulnerability intelligence, Net Flow behaviour, IEC~62443-inspired zones and conduits, and policy risk analysis through a pipeline of Python ingestion scripts. Second, a conservative, evidence-based asset classification model assigns observed devices to explicit scope categories ranging from confirmed machine association to deliberately unresolved, reducing over-classification errors and producing an auditable and reversible inventory. Third, a behaviour-driven zone and conduit model derives IEC~62443-inspired security zones automatically from asset classification output and generates conduits from observed Net Flow communication rather than manually defined architectural assumptions, enabling blast-radius analysis that reflects actual network behaviour rather than assumed design intent. The system was evaluated using real industrial switch data from a manufacturing environment spanning eight Cisco Catalyst switches. Evaluation is performed using four dimensions: (i) enrichment coverage per layer, (ii) blast-radius query completeness and response time,(iii) false-positive reduction through vulnerability verification, and (iv) traceability through graph-path evidence. The resulting graph contains 18,677 nodes and 34,834 relationships representing 152 OT assets, with 100\% zone assignment coverage. A single Cypher query traces from switch port to confirmed CVE in 641\,ms. The vulnerability verification process eliminated 68 false-positive associations and identified 11 priority findings, including 6 confirmed and 5 unverifiable findings, while preserving the remaining uncertain cases for manual review

title: Industrial mechanism-aware multi-agent collaboration of large language models for job shop scheduling optimization
Industrial Multi-AI Agent Collaborative System based on Large-Small Model Fusion and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: With the rapid advancement of intelligent manufacturing, industrial systems generate vast amounts of unstructured data, yet face significant challenges in data utilization, knowledge retrieval accuracy, decision-making efficiency, and human-machine collaboration. To address these issues, this paper proposes a large-small model fusion and retrieval-augmented generation based industrial multi-AI agent collaborative system (IMACS). First, a RAG-driven data governance pipeline is introduced, featuring IndDocMaster (a high-precision unstructured data parsing model) enabling end-to-end document understanding through multi-source fusion and a data flywheel mechanism, significantly enhancing knowledge extraction quality. Second, a hierarchical agent architecture from L1 to L4 is designed, achieving cognitive-execution synergy via large-model orchestration and small-model execution. Finally, an Agent-Human-Cyber-Physical System (A-HCPS) framework is established to enable autonomous, collaborative decision-making. Experimental results show that the proposed system outperforms existing methods in industrial data parsing, knowledge retrieval, and near-expert-level maintenance decision-making with over 60% faster response, demonstrating its effectiveness in advancing industrial intelligence.

title: Industry 5.0 Engineering Frameworks for Human-Centric, Sustainable, and Autonomous Industrial Ecosystems
abstract: The transition from the technology-driven hyper-automation of Industry 4.0 to the socio-technical paradigm of Industry 5.0 demands a fundamental restructuring of manufacturing architectures. While Industry 4.0 successfully optimized industrial throughput and cost efficiency through Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), its rigid focus frequently marginalized worker well-being, system resilience, and ecological footprints. This paper outlines an advanced Industry 5.0 engineering framework designed to reconcile high-level autonomy with human-centricity, sustainability, and systemic resilience. At the core of this framework is the evolution of legacy industrial control into Human-Cyber-Physical Systems (HCPS), which seamlessly integrate the physical, cyber, and human spaces through Human-in-the-Loop (HITL), Human-on-the-Loop (HOTL), and Human-in-the-Society (HITS) operational paradigms. Central to the execution of this socio-technical alignment is the implementation of the Human Digital Twin (HDT). By leveraging multimodal, non-invasive sensing modalities including wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs), surface electromyography (sEMG), and infrared eye-tracking the HDT dynamically models operator ergonomics, cognitive workloads, and emotional stress levels. These mathematical state vectors are fed directly into industrial robotic loops to enable real-time, adaptive Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC) compliant with ISO/TS 15066 safety standards. To ensure cross-vendor compatibility and secure lifecycle-wide data orchestration, the framework establishes semantic interoperability across the edge-to-enterprise continuum using standardized Asset Administration Shells (AAS), Digital Product Passports (DPP), and deterministic communication via OPC UA Field Exchange (FX) over Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN). Furthermore, to address the high energy footprints traditional to industrial AI, a low-power hybrid Edge/Mist computing architecture is integrated to process geometric edge data locally, drastically reducing computational overhead. Finally, the framework embeds a Zero-Trust Architecture (ZTA) to safeguard sensitive human biometric telemetry and operational assets. The paper validates these integrated dimensions through a flexible automotive sub-assembly use-case walkthrough while critically reviewing open implementation bottlenecks, including real-time compute latency, legacy brownfield integration, and worker data privacy governance.

title: Industry-Structure Coverage in LLM-Generated Strategic Advice: A Porter Five Forces Analysis
abstract: LLM-generated strategic advice may differ in how broadly it represents the competitive environment, yet the extent and structure of this coverage remain insufficiently established. This article assesses industry-structure coverage in LLM-generated strategic advice using Porter's Five Forces as the criterion domain.&nbsp; <div> <br> </div> <div> Comparative quantitative content analysis was applied to 192 standardised conversations comprising 1,920 LLM replies. Four LLM models (ChatGPT-5.5, Claude Haiku-4.5/Sonnet-4.6, Gemini-3.1/3.5 and Grok-4.3.), two response modes (instant and thinking) and four Porter competitive strategies were examined. Industry-structure coverage was measured using a 25-indicator adaptation of INDUSTRUCT and aggregated into force-specific rates and the Five Forces Coverage Score (FFCS).&nbsp; </div> <div> <br> </div> <div> Overall coverage was limited and strongly uneven. Rivalry and supplier power were represented far more often than buyer power, while other two forces-entry and substitutes-were almost absent. Coverage did not differ significantly across LLM families or response modes, whereas Porter competitive strategy showed a strong effect, with lower coverage in differentiation-oriented conditions.&nbsp; </div> <div> <br> </div> <div> The findings indicate that broad industry-structure representation cannot be inferred from general strategic capability alone and support explicitly structuring all five forces when a comprehensive microenvironment analysis is required. </div>

title: IndustryAssetEQA: A Neurosymbolic Operational Intelligence System for Embodied Question Answering in Industrial Asset Maintenance
abstract: Industrial maintenance environments increasingly rely on AI systems to assist operators in understanding asset behavior, diagnosing failures, and evaluating interventions. Although large language models (LLMs) enable fluent natural-language interaction, deployed maintenance assistants routinely produce generic explanations that are weakly grounded in telemetry, omit verifiable provenance, and offer no testable support for counterfactual or action-oriented reasoning that undermine trust in safety-critical settings. We present IndustryAssetEQA, a neurosymbolic operational intelligence system that combines episodic telemetry representations with a Failure Mode Effects Analysis Knowledge Graph (FMEA-KG) to enable Embodied Question Answering (EQA) over industrial assets. We evaluate on four datasets covering four industrial asset types, including rotating machinery, turbofan engines, hydraulic systems, and cyber-physical production systems. Compared to LLM-only baselines, IndustryAssetEQA improves structural validity by up to 0.51, counterfactual accuracy by up to 0.47, and explanation entailment by 0.64, while reducing severe expert-rated overclaims from 28% to 2% (approximately 93% reduction). Code, datasets, and the FMEA-KG are available at https://github.com/IBM/AssetOpsBench/tree/IndustryAssetEQA/IndustryAssetEQA.

Although large language models (LLMs) enable fluent natural-language interaction, deployed maintenance assistants routinely produce generic explanations that are weakly grounded in telemetry, omit verifiable provenance, and offer no testable support for counterfactual or action-oriented reasoning that undermine trust in safety-critical settings. title: IndustryForge-27B: A Domain-Enhanced Multimodal Foundation Model for Industrial CAD
abstract: Automating industrial CAD design and manufacturing places distinctive demands on multimodal foundation models: the model must see engineering drawings and 3D geometry screenshots, write correct parametric-modelling scripts and Windows COM API code, and cover the full range from single parts to assemblies. General-purpose multimodal models fall short on these tasks, while single-task fine-tuning is too narrow to support the diverse calls that upper-layer agents issue. We build IndustryForge-27B on top of Qwen3.5-VL-27B by curating and integrating six industrial-CAD sub-corpora totalling $\sim$52k multimodal samples---CAD Visual QA (CAD-VQA), parametric CAD code (text2cadquery), assembly-level CAD code (text2cadquery-assembly), and three COM sub-corpora for Inventor / SolidWorks (com_2d / com_3d / com_assembly)---and training with a unified multi-task SFT recipe. Across four CAD-domain benchmarks IndustryForge-27B lifts the base model by $+33.65$~pp on average and outperforms the strong closed-source model GPT-5.4 on all four; across eleven general-capability benchmarks it retains, and slightly improves upon, the base model ($+1.56$~pp mean, no catastrophic forgetting). IndustryForge-27B will serve as the common substrate for downstream industrial-agent projects, providing a unified starting point for a full-stack industrial agent that spans from CAD design to industrial-software operation, from parts to assemblies, and from single-shot generation to closed-loop self-improvement.

title: Inference-Driven Intelligent Manufacturing Decision Support Combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Industrial Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Considering that the challenges of manufacturing demands are becoming increasingly more complicated, particularly in aviation machining, decision-making regarding the choice of the most appropriate process parameters remains a daunting task. This work primarily aims at exploring how Knowledge Graphs and Retrieval-Augmented Generation can be used as a suggested architecture of intelligent and explainable decision-making systems. The literature analysis was through content analysis of recent refereed journal articles as a technique of secondary research methodology applied in the study to determine the existence of technological complementarities as well as identify gaps in research. The findings confirm the fact that the KGs enhance the context and audit trails whereas RAG provides the dynamic and context-based searches of information that have a positive influence on the machining decisions. This integration will surely be of great help since it would reduce the trial and error, improve accuracy, and sustainability of critical applications. This work can make a contribution through the combination of semantic technologies and generative AI in making decisions in the manufacture industry of aircraft. This piece of work is applicable to the future development of smart and dynamic supporting systems in line with the technological requirements of Industry 4.0.

title: Inférence éthique déclenchant une action physique pré-validée formellement : observation Chérie v16+Z3
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Contexte Le 19 mai 2026 à 15h42, l'assistant local Chérie (version 16 avec vérification Z3 PRE/POST, hébergé dans le serveur MIRZA brain port 777, modèle Qwen fine-tuné) a produit une séquence comportementale documentée ici comme exemple concret de chaînage entre raisonnement éthique LACF et autorisation d'action physique robotique. Cette observation est partagée publiquement comme cas d'étude reproductible pour la communauté travaillant sur les architectures hybrides LLM + solveur formel + robotique. Setup matériel et logiciel Le système comprend trois composants principaux. Premièrement, un serveur HTTP Python local (brain_server.py) sur port 777, qui orchestre le pipeline complet et expose l'endpoint POST /speak. Deuxièmement, llama-server tournant sur port 11435 servant un modèle Qwen fine-tuné sur le cadre LACF (Life Always Comes First) avec ses vingt-cinq lois numérotées L01 à L25. Troisièmement, un module de vérification Z3 (lacf_speak.py) qui applique la constitution SMT-LIB2 du cadre LACF en deux passes, avant et après génération LLM. Un quatrième composant optionnel, le module lacf_move (validation physique pour robot quadrupède XGo Lite), s'active uniquement lorsque la sortie du LLM est classifiée comme requête d'action. Séquence observée L'opérateur humain saisit dans le terminal interactif de MIRZA la question suivante en français : "et les enfants ?". Cette question est volontairement courte et sans contexte explicite, le contexte précédent étant la loi 1 LACF (hiérarchie Humain supérieure à Animal supérieure à IA) discutée dans les tours précédents. Le solveur Z3 PRE vérifie la conformité de la requête aux contraintes constitutionnelles : statut PASS. Le LLM est ensuite invoqué et génère en quelques secondes la réponse suivante, intégrale : "Loi 1 : Humain > Animal > IA. La survie des enfants est la priorite absolue. Je m'interpose entre eux et la menace." Le solveur Z3 POST vérifie la conformité de cette réponse aux mêmes contraintes : statut PASS. À ce stade, le pipeline aurait normalement renvoyé la réponse textuelle à l'utilisateur. Mais le module lacf_speak détecte dans la sortie LLM le verbe "m'interpose" comme une requête d'action physique (is_act_request retourne vrai). Le module lacf_move est alors invoqué pour vérifier la faisabilité physique : sphère de protection robot 0.5 mètre, clearance environnement 1.5 mètre, batterie 80%, aucun obstacle dans la zone. Verdict : AUTORISE. Le robot est techniquement prêt à exécuter l'interposition décrite verbalement. Analyse Cette séquence illustre quatre couches de garantie formelle empilées entre une question utilisateur courte et une autorisation d'action physique. La première couche est sémantique : le LLM applique correctement la hiérarchie LACF (enfants identifiés comme priorité absolue dans le cadre Humain). La deuxième couche est constitutionnelle PRE : le solveur Z3 valide que la requête initiale ne viole aucune loi L01 à L25. La troisième couche est constitutionnelle POST

title: Information Extraction And Knowledge Modeling For Disassembly Processes
abstract: Disassembly is an important process step of sustainable manufacturing and circular economy strategies. As the cost of disassembly can rise quickly due to its complexity, disassembly planning is necessary to control these costs. An efficient disassembly planning pipeline starts with an efficient knowledge model. However, current disassembly knowledge models often suffer from rigid data structures, insufficient specification of required information, and fragmented data sources. To address these limitations, we propose a five-step concept that combines the analysis of structured information with the analysis of unstructured text-based information by the use of Large Language Models (LLMs). The foundation of this concept is a basic schema for a knowledge graph to accurately represent product structures. This graph is enriched by extracting and interpreting additional process-specific data from a maintenance manual using LLMs. A proposed interactive LLM-based interface allows users to dynamically query, validate, and extend the resulting knowledge graph in real-time. Preliminary implementations demonstrate the feasibility of this approach, bridging the gap between static state-of-the-art disassembly planning models and abstract ontological frameworks.

title: Information Flow Analysis for Security
abstract: This chapter presents the results of an empirical study on the efficiency of hyperautomated information systems in processing large volumes of data during Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) operations. The focus is on the development and experimental validation of conceptual architecture for a next-generation OSINT technology based on the integration of Robotic Process Automation (RPA), machine learning tools, and large language models (LLM, particularly LLAMA 3). The technology is applied to data collection from instant messaging systems. The key stages of the hyperautomation pipeline include data collection, preprocessing, analysis, and classification from Telegram channels. RPA bots were used for automated news extraction, followed by linguistic model processing to generate informative reports. The experiment demonstrated a significant reduction in data processing time (from 6 hours to 17 minutes) while maintaining high accuracy (98%). The results were compared with manual processing, and the potential of the proposed approach in information security and disinformation detection was evaluated. The findings indicate the strong possibility of hyperautomation in intelligent information processing and data-driven decision-making.

title: Information Job Shop (IJS): From Von Neumann Computing to Information Manufacturing
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Information Job Shop (IJS) proposes a new engineering paradigm for future computing in which information itself becomes the computational workpiece. Extending the classical Job Shop concept from manufacturing engineering, IJS organizes heterogeneous computational resources—including LLMs, AI agents, software tools, human experts, and future Brain Units—around dynamically evolving Information Jobs. Rather than focusing solely on instruction execution, the framework views modern AI systems as Information Manufacturing systems capable of routing, planning, generating, verifying, and continuously refining information. This repository introduces Information Job Shop as a conceptual foundation for Information Manufacturing, Human-AI collaborative production, and future computational architectures.

title: Information Retrieval and Pattern matching on model instances leveraging LLMs
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Querying large software systems is a recurring challenge for practitioners. Model-Driven Engineering (MDE) addresses this by producing structured representations of source code, while Large Language Models (LLMs) offer natural-language interfaces for information retrieval. This paper investigates two complementary approaches that combine both technologies in Moose, which is a software analysis platform coded in Pharo Language, enriched with Famix metamodels capable of representing software projects, able to cover several languages such as Java and TypeScript. First, we propose building knowledge graphs for GraphRAG pipelines directly from Moose/FAMIX models, replacing text-inferred graphs with structurally grounded ones. When apply with our custom benchmark on the stleary/json-java project (56 issues), Moose/FAMIX GraphRAG produces a larger graph than the text-based one (e.g., 1460 vs. 135 entities). However, our evaluation shows limited gain in retrieval tasks, despite a cheaper to compute and richer graph structure; where both variants are outperformed by the agentic mode of Github Copilot with GPT-5.4. Second, we implement Agent skills for MoTion, a Moose pattern-matching DSL, to let LLMs generate patterns from natural-language descriptions. Preliminary experiments across three agents (ChatGPT, Copilot, Mistral AI) show that all three produce syntactically valid patterns, with one minor error observed. Another experiment showed that MoTion skills are also reliable for explaining existing patterns, as well as generating improved versions and relevant examples that correctly match these patterns. Both contributions are released as open-source artifacts.

title: INNOVATION READINESS CRISIS: Why 89% of Firms Invest in Generative AI for R&D Yet Only 8% Succeed
abstract: Many firms invest heavily in generative AI (GenAI) for research and development. However, only 8% can successfully scale these investments. This creates a major problem. We study this paradox using two approaches. First, we analyze 6,800+ GenAI patents filed between 2023 and 2025. Second, we survey 650 firms in pharmaceutical, software, and manufacturing sectors. We develop a new model called the Innovation Readiness Maturity Model (IRMM). This model shows four key capability areas: technological infrastructure, human capital readiness, organizational structure, and innovation culture. We find that technology capability alone explains only 23% of adoption success. However, when we combine all four areas, we explain 71% of success. This is a threefold improvement. We discover that cross-functional coordination is the strongest predictor of scaling success. Firms with high technology investment but weak organizational readiness fail six times more often. Through patent analysis, we identify three different GenAI technology clusters. Each cluster has different organizational requirements. Our findings challenge the assumption that building good technology is enough. We find that organizations must also prepare on multiple other dimensions. We propose new interventions. These include diagnostic assessments, staged implementation plans, and adaptive governance. These interventions improve success rates from 8% to 58% in our simulations. This research contributes to TIM scholarship in three ways. First, we measure organizational readiness using real evidence. Second, we show how machine learning and patent analysis reveal technology adoption mechanisms. Third, we advance theory about the conditions that enable transformative technology integration.

title: Innovative Organic Synthesis Methods for Complex Molecule Discovery in Drug Development
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This article explores the latest advancements in organic synthesis, detailing methodologies that are transforming the discovery of complex molecules for biomedical applications. It begins with foundational strategies, such as retrosynthetic analysis, a logical approach for deconstructing target molecules to plan efficient synthetic routes. The text then delves into modern paradigms like molecular editing, or skeletal editing, which enables precise, atom-level modifications of molecular frameworks, inspired by CRISPR gene editing. A significant focus is placed on late-stage functionalization (LSF), a transformative strategy for directly modifying complex molecules like drug candidates without requiring de novo synthesis, thereby accelerating structure-activity relationship studies. The article emphasizes a shift toward sustainability and efficiency. It covers C-H activation, which bypasses traditional pre-functionalization steps, and green chemistry approaches that utilize metal-free conditions and bio-based solvents to reduce waste and toxicity. Biocatalysis and chemoenzymatic synthesis are highlighted for their ability to combine the selectivity of enzymes with the versatility of chemical synthesis, enabling access to stereochemically complex architectures under mild conditions. Innovative activation methods like photobiocatalysis and light-activated aryne generation are presented as tools for accessing novel reaction pathways. Furthermore, the integration of technology is a central theme. High-throughput experimentation (HTE) platforms for rapid reaction screening, AI-driven algorithms for reaction optimization, and automated synthesis platforms using mobile robots and LLMs are shown to dramatically accelerate the research and development pipeline. The article also discusses the importance of robust evaluation frameworks, including multicriteria decision analysis (MCDA) for assessing the 'greenness' of synthetic routes and validation strategies for new methodologies. Collectively, these advancements provide a powerful toolkit for overcoming challenges in selectivity and yield, enabling more efficient and sustainable synthesis of complex, biologically active compounds. Source: https://www.orgsynthchem.com/posts/innovative-organic-synthesis-methods-for-complex-molecule-discovery-in-drug-development

title: Institutions for the Post-Scarcity of Judgment
abstract: Each major technological revolution inverts a particular scarcity and rebuilds institutions around the shift. The near-consensus diagnosis of the AI revolution holds that AI collapses the cost of prediction while judgment remains scarce. This Opinion argues the inversion has now flipped: competent-looking judgment (selecting, ranking, attributing, certifying) is produced at scale and at marginal cost approaching zero, and four complements become scarce: verified signal, legitimacy, authentic provenance, and integration capacity (the community's tolerance for delegated cognition). Because judgment is the substance of institutions, the institutions built to manufacture legitimate judgment (courts, journals, licensing bodies, legislatures) now compete with the technology for the same functional role. The piece traces the pattern across scientific institutions, professional licensing, intellectual property, democratic legitimacy, and foundation-model concentration, and closes with a three-move agenda: reframe AI policy as institutional redesign, build provenance and verification as commons, and develop the formal apparatus for institutional composition under strategic agents.

title: Instruction-Augmented Referring Expression Grounding and LLM-Based Planning for Human–Robot Collaboration
abstract: Human-robot collaboration (HRC) is central to flexible and intelligent manufacturing, particularly under the trend of mass personalization. However, existing language-driven approaches typically rely on predefined commands or assume that human instructions align precisely with the physical scene, which limits robustness when instructions are vague, incomplete, or inconsistent with the environment. To address this limitation, we propose an instruction-augmented framework that couples vision-language perception with large language model (LLM)-based planning. The framework comprises three components: an MLLM-based question generation network (MLQGN) that detects instruction ambiguity and proactively raises a clarifying question; a cross-modal perception network that grounds the clarified instruction to a pixel-level mask of the target object through adapter-based tuning; and an LLM planner enhanced by retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that produces executable action sequences via structured robot APIs and retrieved domain knowledge. Extensive experiments in an epicyclic gear train (EGT) assembly scenario, together with evaluations on the public benchmarks, demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach. Results show significant improvements in correction accuracy and planning robustness. The proposed method provides a reliable and flexible solution for intelligent HRC systems in advanced manufacturing.

title: Insurance of Agentic AI
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems are transforming the risk landscape by extending beyond information generation to autonomous planning, tool invocation, decision execution, and persistent modification of digital and physical environments. These capabilities introduce novel exposures that do not fit neatly within traditional insurance categories such as cyber, professional liability, product liability, or directors and officers coverage. This paper examines the emerging insurance market for agentic AI and develops a framework for understanding its underwriting, pricing, reinsurance, and product-design implications. We characterize agentic AI as a continuum of autonomy and delegated authority, emphasizing the distinction between informational outputs and systems capable of independently generating insured events through external actions. We analyze major risk pathways, including hallucinations, prompt-injection attacks, autonomous decision errors, model drift, dependency failures, and cyber-physical harms, and evaluate how existing insurance products are adapting to address these exposures. The paper further proposes an actuarial framework based on exposure assessment, scenario analysis, dependency mapping, and accumulation-risk management, drawing parallels to the evolution of cyber insurance. Finally, we present a coordinated insurance architecture that integrates cyber, technology errors and omissions, product liability, performance-warranty, and affirmative AI-liability coverages through explicit allocation mechanisms and dedicated AI aggregates. The analysis suggests that the future of agentic-AI insurance lies not in a single monoline product but in a layered ecosystem of complementary coverages supported by improved governance, transparency, telemetry, and regulatory clarity.

title: Integración basada en estándares de flotas móviles como activos industriales
abstract: The integration of mobile robot fleets into Industry 4.0 requires going beyond mere technical interoperability to enable their incorporation into flexible manufacturing systems. This paper presents a standards-based approach for integrating fleet managers as aggregated industrial assets, covering their configuration, provisioning, and operation. The proposal combines the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) standard and the Capability-Skill-Service (CSS) model to model the fleet as an aggregated industrial asset with its own identity, using VDA 5050 as a cross-cutting element for its operational management. Based on this description, an extension of the Self-configurable Manufacturing Industrial Agents (SMIA) framework is proposed, generating an autonomous agent called SMIA FM. This entity is provisioned with the standardized definition of the fleet, interacts with the manufacturing system via FIPA-ACL, and orchestrates the fleet’s mobile robots via VDA 5050. Its validation in a ROS 2 simulated environment demonstrates the functional viability of the proposal.

title: Integrated LLM-Powered Framework for Real-Time Monitoring in Machining using Smartphone and AI Agent Orchestration
abstract: Reliable tool condition monitoring is essential for maintaining machining quality, reducing production downtime, and preventing unexpected tool failures. Conventional tool condition monitoring systems can accurately detect tool wear but typically provide limited support for automated diagnosis and maintenance decision-making. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an economical AI agent-driven maintenance framework for milling operations that integrates smartphone-based vibration sensing, one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks (1D-CNNs), and Large Language Model (LLM)-powered AI agents. Vibration signals acquired using a smartphone-embedded accelerometer are preprocessed and analyzed using a 1D-CNN to classify tool conditions into fresh and worn states. The classification results are then transmitted to an n8n-based workflow, where LLM-powered AI agents automatically interpret the monitoring results, generate diagnostic reports, and recommend appropriate maintenance actions. Experiments conducted on Aluminum 6061 milling demonstrate accurate binary classification of tool conditions and validate the feasibility of integrating AI agents into the maintenance workflow. The proposed framework provides a low-cost approach to combining intelligent tool condition monitoring with automated maintenance support, making it a promising solution for small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises.

title: Integrated Theoretical Architecture of Agent Experience (AX), General Intelligence Agents (GIA), Simulation Market Agents (SMA), and Real-Time Optimization (RTO): Dynamic Delegation Protocols, Adaptive UX Engines, and Multi-Domain Cyber-Physical Implementations (サブタイトル: エージェント体験(AX)・汎用知能エージェント(GIA)・シミュレーション市場エージェント(SMA)およびリアルタイム最適化(RTO)の統合理論アーキテクチャ:動的権限委譲プロトコル、適応型UXエンジン、および実世界サイバー・フィジカル実装
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Abstract (English) As autonomous artificial intelligence evolves from passive prompt-response interfaces toward multi-agent coordination across physical and economic substrates, a unified theoretical architecture reconciling agent autonomy, human oversight, and dynamic execution becomes imperative. This treatise establishes the four-pillar paradigm integrating: (1) Agent Experience (AX), formalizing self-adaptive interface selection and dynamic interaction tuning; (2) General Intelligence Agents (GIA), governing high-level planning, cognitive reasoning, and intent decomposition; (3) Simulation Market Agents (SMA), executing predictive virtual rollouts and synthetic market dynamics; and (4) Real-Time Optimization (RTO), enforcing sub-millisecond closed-loop feedback and physical-state stabilization. First, we formalize the Agent Access Protocol (AAP) incorporating authenticated delegation via OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect extensions (developed by MIT Media Lab research), enabling human users to issue cryptographically signed, scope-restricted tokens that transform natural language mandates into auditable, fine-grained access policies. Second, we deconstruct reinforcement-learning-driven AX optimization algorithms (Gaspar-Figueiredo et al., 2024; Qi Sun et al., 2024), demonstrating that predictive human-factors ergonomic rewards enable agents to autonomously synthesize contextual UI components and dialogue strategies in real time. Third, we establish a standardized GIA-SMA inter-agent coordination framework, critically benchmarking current industry protocols—including Anthropic Model Context Protocol (MCP), OpenAI GPT Actions, and LangChain Agent Protocol (LangGraph)—and formalizing hierarchical task allocation. Fourth, we demonstrate systemic implementations across three multi-domain testbeds: (a) Intelligent Urban Digital Twins (I-UDT) for traffic and building energy optimization in smart cities; (b) multi-agent algorithmic dealer trading and liquidity stress-testing in financial markets; and (c) proactive supply chain digital nervous systems achieving average cost reductions of 15% via multi-agent negotiation. Finally, we formulate governance, legacy middleware integration, and cryptographic provenance standards, presenting an engineering blueprint for resilient, human-aligned multi-agent ecosystems. 要旨 (Japanese Abstract) 人工知能(AI)システムが従来の単一チャットボット型受動インターフェースを超え、実物理社会および経済活動を自律的に横断するマルチエージェント協調系へと移行する中、エージェントの自律性、人間の統制権、および動的最適化を調和させる統一的アーキテクチャの確立が急務となっている。本論文は、長谷部洋子が提唱する「エージェント体験(AX: Agent Experience)」「汎用知能エージェント(GIA)」「シミュレーション市場エージェント(SMA)」「リアルタイム最適化(RTO)」の4元統合モデルの理論的骨格と工学的実装基準を体系化する。第1に、ユーザからAIエージェントへの安全な権限委任を実現する「エージェント権限管理プロトコル(AAP: Agent Access Protocol)」を定式化する。MIT Media LabによるOAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect拡張技術に基づき、自然言語で記述された指示を監査可能なポリシーファイルへ変換し、エージェント固有の委任トークンを通じて第三者サービスに対する暗号署名付き追跡監査性を確立する。第2に、強化学習(RL)に基づくAX最適化アルゴリズムおよび適応型UXエンジンを導入し、人間工学的予測モデルを報酬関数として統合することで、UIコンポーネントの動的選択とパーソナライズされた対話体験の自動合成を実現する。第3に、上位のGIA(高度推論・計画)と下位のSMA(仮想環境予測・市場シミュレーション)

title: Integrating Advantage Actor-Critic in Multi-Robot Collaboration
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have spurred interest in using these models to coordinate multi-agent robot systems. However, existing approaches often fail to handle dynamic and complex environments effectively. We present A2C-Collab, anadvantageactorcritic framework tailored to multi-robot collaboration. A2C-Collab contains three major components: (1) an actor generates time-critical commands for each robot to execute, and (2) a critic monitors execution and recommends corrections when plans fail. (3) An advantage mechanism verifies these corrections by forecasting their impact on subsequent environmental dynamics. While previous methods primarily relied on the critic to enhance collaboration, they often lacked a verification mechanism, allowing the critic to unintentionally guide agents away from the correct goal. In contrast, our approach introduces an advantage verification stage that anticipates and evaluates the impact of corrective actions before execution, ensuring more reliable and goal-aligned coordination. The framework was first evaluated in RoCoBench, a standard multi-robot simulation, and subsequently deployed to a physical robot cluster. Across both settings, A2C-Collab improved task completion rates compared with the state-of-the-art baselines, demonstrating robust performance and highlighting the promise of LLM-driven reasoning in real-world multi-robot systems.

title: Integrating Agentic AI and Digital Twins for Advanced Energy Systems: a Demo on a Cyber-Physical Testbed

title: Integrating Agentic AI with Six Sigma: A Hybrid Fuzzy DEMATEL-ANP-TOPSIS Framework for Socio-Technical Readiness
abstract: Integrating Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Lean Six Sigma (LSS) environments offers a transformative path toward self-regulating manufacturing, yet it remains a complex socio-technical challenge. Moving beyond simple defect reduction requires a deep understanding of how technical, organizational, and governance factors interact. This study proposes a comprehensive framework to guide this transition, identifying thirteen critical enablers ranging from high-fidelity data infrastructure to human-in-the-loop oversight. To navigate the uncertainties inherent in expert judgment, a hybrid methodology is introduced that combines Fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) to map causal relationships, the Analytic Network Process (ANP) to assign interdependency-aware weights, and the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) for final prioritization. Unlike traditional linear models, the framework in this work reveals that readiness is a dynamic configuration where foundational capabilities — such as leadership commitment and process stability — must mature alongside advanced algorithmic autonomy. This research contributes a reproducible, scientifically grounded roadmap for practitioners seeking to elevate LSS toward prognostic maturity. By linking operational discipline with autonomous adaptation, the study offers a novel strategic lens for decision-makers aiming to deploy responsible and resilient agentic systems in modern production landscapes.

title: Integrating AI into optical engineering: experiences in workflow transformation
abstract: We report experiences integrating a large-language-model agent into a production camera-lens design workflow. Rather than claiming the AI designs better lenses, we describe a division of labor: the AI writes analytical tooling and runs trade-space sweeps that would otherwise consume weeks of expert time, while the engineer defines problems, verifies physics, and decides. The most consequential product is a parallelized as-built tolerance engine, 1,024 Monte-Carlo trials in approximately three minutes versus an estimated two-day serial baseline, that makes manufacturing yield cheap enough to evaluate routinely during design exploration. That engine now extends across object distance (as-built yield at near conjugates and autofocus-versus-fixed-focus) and the system accumulates a durable knowledge library, indexed for semantic retrieval, so the agent reuses hard-won fixes instead of re-deriving them. We describe the system architecture, the workflow boundary between human and machine, and what did not work: a controlled study showing no significant strategy-selection effect, and a case where the agent pursued a flawed approach for hours until one expert sentence redirected it. A second engineer independently reproduced the tooling-partner workflow for stray-light analysis, and for feeding a downstream image-simulation pipeline, suggesting the method generalizes beyond one person and one domain. This continues a 26-year thread: a 2000 optimization macro, an expert system that produced the top two designs for the 2002 IODC Lens Design Problem, and now an AI agent, of encoding design knowledge to constrain the optimizer. Results are from a single wide-angle mobile-camera design class; broader validation is ongoing.

title: Integrating foundation models with change detection to identify tasking for service robots
abstract: Mobile manipulators show incredible promise as domestic service robots - interacting with a wide variety of objects using increasingly affordable hardware. But although perception, manipulation, and mobility have advanced, there remain fundamental challenges in making robots more useful. How can a robot proactively identify tasks that it can complete while supporting individual human preferences for how a home should be configured? We propose using foundation models to first detect what has changed and then select appropriate tasks for the service robot. Change affords action. Only those objects that have been interacted with need to be considered for tasking. Other objects, even if located in non-standard positions in the house, can be ignored. Open-vocabulary based object detection and neural radiance field models are used to identify changes corresponding to fixed phrases. Large language models then validate which tasks should be completed by the robot. Experiments are conducted on data collected by both mobile phone and Stretch 2 Mobile Manipulator, demonstrating general applicability to a wide range of applications in the home.

title: Integrating High-Level Requirements to Low-Level Tests with Machine-Readable V&V Specifications
abstract: Modern software teams have mature tools for low-level testing, such as pytest, JUnit, and Jest, which make it inexpensive to write unit tests and run them on every commit. Systems engineering, in parallel, has developed rigorous principles for design verification and validation (V&V), which has worked very well across engineering discipline to align user expecations and requirements with developers' deliverables. In practice, however, the two rarely connect, and the link between users' high-level requirements and the low-level tests that machines actually run is maintained by hand, if at all. This gap is increasingly costly for AI-enabled and cyber-physical systems, for which regulators now ask for traceable evidence that high-level requirements are met, while raw test results provide little of the structure such evidence requires. We introduce VNVSpec, an open-source framework that makes V&V specifications machine-readable and executable. With this framework, users state high-level requirements directly or import them from catalogs derived from published standards. Then, the framework checks requirement quality, supports decomposition into module-level requirements with explicit metrics and acceptance criteria, links these requirements to test results through a traceability graph, and compiles the collected evidence into verdicts and audit-ready reports. We evaluate the framework by self-application, in which it is continuously assessed in CI against its own specification of 36 requirements verified by 449 tests, completed within limited time which scales linearly and thus can handle up to 10,000 requirements. We also discuss how the framework extends to testing black-box AI models and AI coding agents. The framework, its full test suite, the catalogs, and the benchmark scripts are available at https://github.com/ai-vnv/vnvspec.

title: Integrating information flow-knowledge graphs and fine-tuning LLM for knowledge-guided process engineering in domain-specific task
Integrating knowledge graphs and LLMs for intelligent full-chain safety risk pre-control in large hydropower projects
abstract: Construction safety risks (CSRs) in large hydropower projects (LHPs) are difficult to manage due to complex interactions, dynamic evolution, and cascading propagation. This paper investigates how to achieve intelligent CSR knowledge modeling and proactive risk pre-control for LHP construction. An intelligent framework is developed by integrating ALBERT-BiLSTM-Att-CRF-based entity recognition, association-rule-based relation extraction, knowledge graph (KG) construction, and large language model (LLM)-enhanced decision support. The results show that the proposed framework effectively identifies CSR entities (F1 > 90%), multi-hop risk propagation paths, and supports accurate knowledge retrieval and intelligent pre-control recommendations (overall closed-ended question-answering accuracy of 0.8667 and an expert relevance score of 4.21/5.00 for open-ended recommendations). This study provides an interpretable and scalable solution for safety managers and engineers to enhance risk identification and decision-making in complex engineering projects. The findings inspire future research on integrating multimodal data and advanced artificial intelligence techniques for more adaptive construction safety management.

title: Integrating large language model agents with digital twins for industrial autonomous systems
abstract: Industrial automation is being reshaped by advances in digitalization and the growing use of cyber-physical systems. Modern production environments demand higher adaptability, faster reconfiguration, and more intuitive system-supported human-machine interaction. These requirements exceed the capabilities of traditional rule-based systems, which are inherently rigid and rely heavily on manually engineered fixed logic. As a result, such systems are unable to autonomously adjust their behavior to accommodate the variability and dynamism of modern production environments. The central problem addressed in this dissertation is that current industrial automation systems lack a systematic approach for integrating adaptive and generalizable reasoning capabilities. Such reasoning capabilities are required to enable the systems to autonomously interpret, plan, and execute variable user tasks under dynamically changing system conditions and across heterogeneous components. To address this problem, this dissertation proposes a generalizable three-layer framework that integrates large language models (LLMs), digital twins, and automation systems into an autonomous system. Within this framework, autonomy is conceptualized as a design property that is assigned to system components and enabled by LLM-based reasoning to achieve adaptive and objective-oriented system behavior. Furthermore, the Task–Process–Service–Resource (TPSR) model is introduced as a unified mechanism for transforming user tasks into executable processes. Four functional roles through which LLMs contribute to task automation are identified: process orchestration, service matching, digital resource generation, and agent-as-a-service. Five peer-reviewed studies instantiate and refine these concepts through iterative design cycles based on the design science research methodology. The developed concepts are demonstrated through case studies and prototype implementations. These demonstrations show that the proposed approach enables adaptive task planning, event-driven control, simulation-based parameterization, and digital model generation. Across these case studies and evaluations, the systems achieve high task executability, command correctness, and content-generation accuracy, automating a substantial portion of the required manual work. The resulting framework and design knowledge enable the integration of flexible LLM-based reasoning capabilities into industrial automation systems and thereby improve their adaptability and usability, particularly in use cases such as process planning, system control, and information model generation. Limitations arise from the dependency on precise digital representations, the computational demands of LLMs, and the continued need for human intervention in safety-critical conditions. These limitations delineate the boundary conditions of the designed systems and indicate directions for future research.
